stories.headline: Manu Bhaker suffers another personal loss; grandmother passes away in Rohtak
stories.deck: The grief comes at a difficult time for Manu Bhaker, who is already coping with the recent setback involving her coach Jaspal Rana. The shooter was undergoing training in Bhopal as part of her preparations for the Asian Games when she received news of her grandmother's demise. She immediately left for her native village.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Olympic medallist 
Manu Bhaker
 suffered another personal setback on Tuesday as her 84-year-old grandmother, Daya Kaur, passed away at a private hospital in Rohtak.
Daya Kaur had been admitted to the hospital after experiencing chest pain and was also dealing with age-related health complications. She shared a close bond with Manu and remained one of her biggest sources of affection and support.
The grief comes at a difficult time for Manu, who is already coping with the recent setback involving her coach Jaspal Rana. The shooter was undergoing training in Bhopal as part of her preparations for the 
Asian Games
 when she received news of her grandmother's demise. She immediately left for her native village.
Manu's family was with Daya Kaur during her final hours. Her mother was in Bhopal with Manu, while her father, Mahendra Bhaker, was in Ahmedabad. Other family members were also away, while her aunt was present at the hospital.
Daya Kaur had followed Manu's journey closely, including her historic performance at the Paris Olympics, where Manu became the first Indian athlete since independence to win two medals at a single edition of the Games. She had watched her granddaughter's events from her village and celebrated her success with immense pride.
For Manu, the loss is deeply personal. Family members recall the special bond between the two, with Daya Kaur often pampering her granddaughter and feeding her traditional homemade choorma.
Manu's shooting commitments are now temporarily on hold as she returns home to be with her family. The Indian shooting team is scheduled to leave on Sept 15.
Daya Kaur's last rites will be performed at her native village on Wednesday.

stories.headline: SP-RLD row over chavanni flips open caste fault lines ahead of U.P. poll
stories.deck: The war of words between SP and RLD over political loyalty and caste identity ahead of the upcoming state elections reflects the shifting winds in western Uttar Pradesh
stories.bodyText:
The modest chavanni – the now-obsolete 25-paise coin – is gaining currency in western Uttar Pradesh ahead of the State election following a war of words over loyalty and caste identity between Rashtriya Lok Dal (RLD) president Jayant Chaudhary and his former ally, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav.
The conflict escalated after Mr. Yadav made a veiled jibe targeting Mr. Chaudhary. “We turned a chavanni into a rupee, and yet they left us,” the SP chief said at a recent event in Lucknow. This was a direct reference to Mr. Chaudhary’s own famous 2022 declaration, when he resisted Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) initial overtures during the 2022 poll by saying, “I am not a chavanni that will flip.”
After subsequently flipping to join the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA) before the 2024 Lok Sabha election, Mr. Chaudhary became a prime target for the Opposition.
At the time, he defended the move because the BJP-led government conferred the Bharat Ratna on former Prime Minister and his grandfather, Chaudhary Charan Singh, before the election.
Jat loyalties in the region are broadly governed by farming issues, respect for Mr Chaudhary’s family and Hindutva, and perhaps that’s why Mr. Chaudhary explained his political switch to the electorate during the Lok Sabha election with a cryptic line, “Main palta nahin hoon, maine palti di hai, ise patakhni marna kehte hain (I didn’t turn my back or betray anyone; I executed a strategic move to slam my political rivals.”
The Jats read it in two ways. Those nursing a grudge against Mulayam Singh Yadav – for betraying the trust of his mentor Charan Singh and scuttling his son Ajit Singh’s chances of becoming U.P.’s Chief Minister after the Janata Dal came to power in December 1989 – saw Mr. Chaudhary’s flip to the BJP as a perfect move. And farmers who questioned the silence of the BJP’s Jat face, Sanjeev Balyan, during the farm agitation saw it as a strategic manoeuvre to reclaim Jat politics from the BJP while remaining in the NDA fold. Mr Balyan, who defeated then RLD Supremo Ajit Singh in 2019, lost his seat in 2024.
Two years later, the ground has shifted. In SP’s electoral narrative, Mr. Chaudhary is in the Rajya Sabha because of its largesse and should have resigned when the RLD joined the NDA. The breakdown happened over the number of seats, but SP sympathisers underline that the BJP left only two seats for RLD in the Lok Sabha poll while the SP was ready to give five more. Out of nine MLAs, RLD has two Muslim MLAs in the Jat belt, and the SP seems keen to win them and their community support base. The party is also reaching out to Gurjars to make a choice.
Despite joining hands with the BJP, Mr. Chaudhary hasn’t given up on his bhaichara plank, but the current friction will make it difficult for him to hold on to it. It is favourable for the BJP as it will help it polarise the election in western U.P. For, after RLD’s rise in 2022, Muslim farmers once again saw Jat farmers as their shield.
There is a section in the ruling party in the State that feels that the tie-up with the RLD didn’t help, as the INDIA bloc secured six of the eight seats in the heart of the sugarcane belt in 2024. But observers feel the BJP’s central leadership bought peace at the U.P. border by aligning with RLD, and in that sense it is a successful move because the Jat farmers had packed their lathis and parked their tractors off the National Highway 9. In its recently constituted Parliamentary Board, RLD has included Yudhvir Singh, farmer leader and the general secretary of the Tikait faction of the Bharatiya Kisan Union, as a special invitee.
RLD insiders believe the party stemmed the impending disaster from the BJP’s internal fight and is seeking a bigger slice of the pie. With the SP, RLD contested 33 Assembly seats. It helps that the Jats are agitated against the SP because now even those who feel Chaudhary Charan Singh saw Mulayam Singh Yadav as his political heir in his lifetime cannot ignore the SP chief’s personal attacks. They are using the hukka bharna (doing the bidding), a cultural metaphor of subservience, to describe Mulayam Singh’s respect for his mentor.
Meanwhile, SP’s Jat leaders are getting into semantics to deflect the issue and are invoking Charan Singh, who cautioned against the entry of diya bati (the symbol of the Jan Sangh) in villages.
There was a time when Mr. Chaudhary described the alliance between SP, Bahujan Samaj Party, and RLD as a tie-up that best reflected the State’s social fabric. He resisted projecting himself as a Jat leader in public. However, the current fracas, where SP State president Shyamlal Pal mocked the RLD leadership by saying that they “taught them (Jats) the ABCD of politics”, has forced him to invoke his Jat background through a thinly veiled post on X, where he said it would have been better had people named him rather than targeting the community.
Playing on the letters, Mr. Chaudhary remarked last week at a rally in Saharanpur, “G for Ganna and J, you know”, warning the RLD would trap the SP right between the two. SP’s Gurjar leadership responded, “If J stands for Jat, G has to be Gurjar.”
Political observers feel after resisting for a long time, Mr. Chaudhary had to bow to a large chunk of his vote bank’s demand, which saw the community’s future with the BJP after the Muzaffarnagar communal riots. However, after two years in government, where he is Minister of State for Education, the same section that didn’t support him enough when he led protests against the Agniveer recruitment is questioning his silence on Gen-Z protests against paper leaks and rewinding reels of his speeches during the farmer protests and the police action against him in Hathras after the rape and murder of a Dalit girl. The recent murder of Haryanvi singer Ankit Balyan in Shamli is seen as yet another provocation for him to get into ‘action’ mode.
The big question in the days to come is whether Mr. Chaudhary will shed the chavanni tag by making the BJP cede seats worth a rupee for him.

stories.headline: Trump bans some Canada goods as trade war swells
stories.deck: The import ban, which targets various alcoholic beverages as well as some dairy products like whey, will come into effect on September 29
stories.bodyText:
The White House ramped up its trade dispute with Canada late on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) by banning the import of certain products, including alcoholic beverages, and raising tariffs on other goods.
A range of Canadian products, from mattresses to motorboats and golf carts, will be subject to a 50% surcharge beginning September 15, stated an executive order by President Donald Trump.
The import ban, which targets various alcoholic beverages as well as some dairy products like whey, will come into effect on September 29, according to other executive orders issued at the same time.
One of the statements of presidential action describes how certain Canadian products will no longer be subject to the 50% tariffs that recently came into effect after bilateral trade negotiations collapsed last month. But the list of these products is significantly shorter, with toilet paper among them.
“President Trump is doing this to make sure, again, that we keep a level playing field, deter retaliation, and of course protect American production,” a senior administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.
The retaliation comes as Ottawa has just imposed new tariffs on U.S. products in response to the duties announced by Washington on August 22.
The senior official said Canadians had been warned that their reaction would escalate the situation.
As justification for the ban on imports of alcohol from Canada, Mr. Trump cited what he called “discriminatory” provincial boycotts of U.S. booze.
Since the start of Mr. Trump’s tariff offensive last year, Canadians have launched a massive boycott of U.S. products: wines and spirits have disappeared from store shelves in most Canadian provinces, which hold a monopoly on their sale.
Earlier Tuesday (September 8, 2026), Mr. Trump threatened to exclude Canadian products from a government procurement program “unless Canada restores full and fair reciprocity for American Farmers and Companies.”
In a social media post, Mr. Trump said he was directing officials “to REMOVE Canadian-origin products from GSA’s Multiple Award Schedules,” referring to a General Services Administration program for long-term contracts. Such schedules account for over $50 billion a year, Mr. Trump added.
U.S. trade lawyer Ryan Majerus said the move could widen the scope of impacted goods beyond those hit by tariffs.

stories.headline: Delhi HC raps Centre for outing survivor's name in its POSH handbook
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: Delhi HC rapped Centre for naming a workplace sexual harassment survivor in a handbook it published on preventing such harassment and dealing with complaints.
“How is the name of the victim disclosed in this? How can you do that? You are the govt of India. You yourself are publishing (handbooks) revealing the name of the victim and you are circulating it. It is on your official website,” Justice Swarana Kanta Sharma said, listing the matter for the next hearing on Wednesday.
Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) handbook was published by Ministry of Women and Child Development. Law prohibits revealing the identity of the survivor of a sexual offence, and doing so is a punishable offence.
HC asked Union govt’s lawyer to come back with the names of officials “responsible for this content” while hearing a petition by the alleged perpetrator, who submitted that the matter has since been settled and therefore, sought directions for removal of his name from the handbook.

Handbook is ‘everywhere and anywhere’ on internet: Lawyer
The petitioner’s counsel submitted that a labour tribunal order arising from the alleged incident has been included in the handbook as an anecdote, revealing the details of not only his identity but the woman’s name as well.
The handbook is “everywhere and anywhere” on the internet, the lawyer said. that the Centre’s counsel submitted that the handbook was published in Nov 2015 for educational purposes, and the parties settled the matter only recently.
“So will it reveal the name of the victim? Even a judgement cannot,” Justice Sharma responded. “For educational purposes you don’t need the victim’s name, right? Even the judges write ‘X’. There are directions of high court. You can’t disclose the name. Now it is punishable,”
HC reminded the counsel as it added that judicial directions to protect a survivor’s identity were in place even before 2015 and the authorities cannot be absolved of their responsibility to follow the law even if a party was acting on it now. The petitioner also sought directions to Google for de-linking and de-indexing the content.

stories.headline: Karnataka records highest-ever power demand for September
stories.bodyText: Karnataka has recorded a power demand of 340 million units (MUs) on Monday, the highest-ever for a day in September.The state has been reporting a drastic increase in power demand due to poor monsoon and rising temperatures.“The demand is usually lower during monsoon but due to poor rains this year, demand from the agricultural sector to power irrigation pumpsets and the residential demand have gone up. On some days, the demand increases by as much as 30%,” Gaurav Gupta, Additional Chief Secretary (Energy), told DH.While demand is increasing, ramping up production has also been challenging, officials noted..Karnataka aims to boost power generation capacity to 66 GW by 2030.Poor monsoon has affected hydropower production in the state while power exchange agreements signed in the last few years have also forced Karnataka to send power to other states.“We had received power from Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and other states during summer through power-exchange agreements. We received power during summer and are supposed to return it during monsoon. Despite poor rains, we have to abide by the agreement and send power. This has also been a challenge,” Energy Minister K J George said.To make up for the shortfall, Karnataka is purchasing power from the Indian Energy Exchange, he added.“We are purchasing power despite high prices on the exchange. However, sometimes, that is also not available. We are trying our best to meet the demand,” George added.Unscheduled power cutsAlthough the department has maintained that steps are in place to ensure there are no power disruptions, citizens complain that unscheduled power cuts — some stretching several hours a day — have increased over the last month.Gupta said some local issues could have caused power outages. “We have put in place measures to ensure there are no outages. We are balancing demand and supply. There are no outages due to lack of power,” he said.

briefs.headline: Nainital Police register FIR against ‘unknown persons’ for performing ‘purification’ of Mallikarjun Kharge’s rally venue
briefs.deck: The development comes after the Congress repeatedly demanded police action against those who performed purification of the rally venue of party’s national president
briefs.bodyText:
Almost a month after ‘shuddhikaran’ (purification) ritual conducted at Haldwani’s Ramlila ground following a rally addressed by Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on August 8, the Nainital Police on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) lodged a First Information Report (FIR) against ‘unknown persons’ for the conduct.
On August 11, members of the Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas Sangathan conducted a ‘shuddhikaran yagna’ (purification yagna) at the venue. Video of the ritual went viral on social media in which all the participants were visible performing the hawan. A few of them also interacted with the media post the event.
Nainital Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Manjunath TC told the media that the FIR was registered against unknown persons on the complaint of Congress worker Anju, who, according to him, was the first person to submit a complaint in connection with the matter.
“We have received various petitions and complaints in this matter....this was also one of them. The FIR was lodged after due diligence,” said the SSP, adding that investigation in the matter would be done by Superintendent of Police (Crime) Jagdish Chandra.
He added that the case had been registered under Sections 196 and 299 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Section 3(1)(R) of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
The development comes after the Congress had repeatedly demanded police action against those who performed purification of the rally venue of party’s national president alleging that the same was done because Mr. Kharge belonged to Dalit community.
The organisers have denied that the ceremony was directed at Mr. Kharge or had any caste motive.
Last week, the police had also lodged a case against Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi over his remarks on Haldwani’s ‘purification’ ritual, with a Scheduled Caste complainant alleging that the comments hurt his sentiments.
The FIR was registered on a complaint by Vinod Kumar Arya and Amit Kumar, who are associated with the Shri Ram Sena Dharmarth Seva Nyas. Mr. Kumar is a member of the Scheduled Caste community.
Mr. Kharge also raised the matter in the Rajya Sabha in the recent monsoon session, demanding cases under laws dealing with untouchability against those who carried out the purification ceremony and calling for their arrest and imprisonment.
Last week, BJP State president Mahendra Bhatt once again stroked the controversy around the ritual after he supported the act and alleged that the same was done as ‘slogans’ were raised at the venue which had polluted the place associated with Lord Ram.
The FIR registration comes after reports suggested that Mr. Gandhi will be in Uttarakhand on September 11 and 12.

briefs.headline: Netanyahu will make quick trip to speak at UN after Mamdani urged his arrest, diplomat says
briefs.deck: Ambassador Danny Danon accused Mayor Zohran Mamdani of “doing politics” when he called the Prime Minister a “war criminal” and called for his arrest
briefs.bodyText:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is making a whirlwind 24-hour trip to speak at the annual UN gathering of world leaders this month because “there is no option” after New York's mayor urged his arrest over the war in Gaza, Israel's UN envoy said on Tuesday (September 8, 2026).
Ambassador Danny Danon accused Mayor Zohran Mamdani of “doing politics” when he called the Prime Minister a “war criminal” and called for his arrest, which he had to withdraw because New York City does not have the authority to take Mr. Netanyahu into custody.
“You know, it became very trendy to do politics by blaming Israel,” Mr. Danon said. He stressed, “For us, it's important the Prime Minister will come.” Netanyahu has become an increasingly polarising figure over Israel's war against Hamas in Gaza.
Mr. Mamdani, whose office did not immediately respond to messages seeking comment on Tuesday (September 8, 2026), has pointed to the arrest warrant issued by the world's top war crimes tribunal against Mr. Netanyahu in November 2024, accusing him and another Israeli official of crimes against humanity.
The International Criminal Court warrant said there was reason to believe Mr. Netanyahu used “starvation as a weapon of warfare” by restricting humanitarian aid and intentionally targeting civilians in the campaign against Hamas – charges Israel denies.
While New York City does not have legal authority to execute an ICC arrest warrant, Mr. Mamdani has encouraged the federal government to do so.
The U.S. and Israel are not members of the court, and the Trump administration has imposed a series of sanctions on ICC staffers in a campaign to dismantle the tribunal.
Mr. Netanyahu is scheduled to arrive in New York late on September 23, address the UN General Assembly on the afternoon of September 24 and fly back to Israel that night, Mr. Danon said.
Mr. Danon noted that the meeting of leaders from the 193 UN member nations is taking place during the Jewish holidays and an election campaign as Mr. Netanyahu tries to keep his job as Prime Minister.
Mr. Danon said protests against Netanyahu would “create more chaos” on New York streets during the high-level meetings the week of September 22-28.
Last year, there was a mass walkout from the UN General Assembly hall when Mr. Netanyahu started to speak from the podium. This year, Mr. Danon said, “I expect that there will be something like another show.” But the ambassador said Mr. Netanyahu is experienced, “and I'm sure he will deliver his speech despite those attempts”.

briefs.headline: UPI-ng the ante: PM Modi wants desi connect with global pay
briefs.bodyText:
MUMBAI: PM Narendra Modi Tuesday called for India to set its own standards and protocols for cross-border payments and directly integrate its payment system with countries where Indian diaspora populations are large and trade volumes significant.
He said India now had a sovereign alternative to the foreign standards under-pinning the existing card-payment architecture and could connect it with the global financial system.
Modi said the move could also reduce the cost of remittances, noting that Indians abroad send the largest volume of money home globally but lose a notable portion to transaction fees. “UPI can deliver substantial savings here as well, allowing funds to reach Indian families far more rapidly,” he said.
His remarks came ahead of the Brics summit, where expanding national and local currency trade is a priority. A proposal seeks to enable retail and trade-settlement interoperability between fast-payment systems by linking UPI with similar networks in other countries. India has been looking at ways to reduce reliance on the dollar for cross-currency trade while Brics has stopped short of referring to the dollar, with the 2025 declaration calling for finding “acceptable mechanisms of financing in local currencies”.
“We have already accomplished this with Singapore. As a result, cross-border transactions between India and Singapore occur as seamlessly as transfers between two neighbourhoods of the same city. We must replicate these integrations across other countries and international markets,” the PM said.
Addressing Global Fintech Fest for the third consecutive year, Modi said India had gr-own 7.8% despite pressure on energy and commodity supply chains and escalating trade tensions. He also cited a Japanese ratings agency upgrading India to the A category, a milestone achieved after three decades. “This reflects how confident the world has become in the structural reforms implemented over the past years. And I reiterate: India’s ‘Reform Express’ will advance at an even faster pace,” he said.
The PM called for stronger cybersecurity, industry-led ethical data-protection stand-ards, a regulatory-industry innovation ecosystem and a fintech consumer-protection index with clear and transparent ratings. He also said the sector needed to diversify beyond payments by expanding credit, insurance, savings, investments and pension products.
Noting that Global Fintech Fest coincided with UPI’s 10th anniversary, Modi said those excluded from formal banking for generations were now driving fintech growth.

Noting that besides fintech energy, Mumbai’s cultural energy was also at its peak thanks to Ganeshotsav festivities around the corner, Modi extended warm wishes. Attending the annual fest for the third consecutive time, Modi said, would be his second “hat trick” — the first being in 2024 when NDA formed govt for a third time.

briefs.headline: Eiffel Tower shuts after staff strike over BAPS visit
briefs.bodyText:
Eiffel Tower in Paris was closed to visitors Monday after staff suddenly went on strike, alleging that female employees were moved from their stations during a visit by a delegation from a Gujarat-based Hindu religious group.
A 100-strong delegation linked to Bochasanwasi Akshar Purushottam Swaminarayan Sanstha (BAPS) had visited Eiffel Tower ahead of Festival of Cultures, marking the consecration of a Swaminarayan Temple in Paris over the weekend.
PTI quoted workers' union representative Diane Davoine as saying women members of the staff were asked to leave their stations as the delegation arrived at the tourism landmark. Confederation Generale du Travail, a national forum of trade unions, alleged that in some cases, women employees were temporarily replaced by male colleagues and told to avoid particular areas till the religious delegation left.
The operating company, Societe d'Exploitation de la tour Eiffel (SETE), said the tower reopened as usual on Tuesday, acknowledging that a BAPS delegation had requested "limited interactions with women" and that the condition "should not have been accepted".
BAPS issued a detailed statement insisting the arrangements were never gender-based. It said the visit was coordinated in advance purely for logistical reasons. 
"Given the size of the group, this visit was coordinated in advance with the Eiffel Tower's management team and was scheduled at the start of normal operating hours specifically to minimise any disruption to staff, other visitors, and the site's regular functioning.

Be respectful · TOI community guidelines
" MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said the matter was purely between the entities concerned.
BAPS regretted any inconvenience caused to employees by the arrangements. "We take seriously the concerns expressed by the Eiffel Tower's employees, and we sincerely regret any inconvenience or discomfort caused to them as a result of the arrangements made for our group's visit."
Paris mayor Emmanuel Gregoire called the employees' anger legitimate. National Assembly President Yael Braun-Pivet said women in France fully occupy public spaces and cannot be told to make themselves invisible. Gender equality minister Aurore Berge called the episode unacceptable, saying no religion is above the Republic's laws. Former PM Gabriel Attal backed Tower's staff, saying no culture or belief can dictate a woman's place.

briefs.headline: Putin meeting PM Modi on Friday; energy, defence high on agenda
briefs.bodyText:
Russia described as illegal and unacceptable the US move to impose 100% tariffs on nations importing Russian oil, while confirming another bilateral meeting between PM Modi and President Vladimir Putin on Friday. Putin is travelling to India this week for his first overseas participation in a BRICS summit since the Russia-Ukraine war started in Feb 2022.
Ahead of the visit, a Kremlin spokesperson said India’s energy imports from Russia were setting new records and both countries also had similar positions on the war. He welcomed India’s intention to facilitate a peaceful resolution of the conflict.
India will host the BRICS summit on Sept 12-13. While China is yet to officially confirm President Xi Jinping’s participation, diplomatic sources said he’s likely to arrive Saturday and have a bilateral meet with Modi the same day.
India & Russia exploring cooperation on rare earths
Modi and Putin had met on Aug 31 on the margins of the SCO summit in Bishkek. In their bilateral meeting Friday, the two will look to ramp up trade, energy and defence ties. Dmitry Peskov, the Russian presidential spokesperson, said that both sides are exploring cooperation on rare earths and also the sale of Sukhoi Su-57 stealth fighter jets to India.
Against the backdrop of Modi’s message to Putin that it was high time the “endless” war was brought to an end, the official said India’s position on Ukraine was aligned with Moscow’s stand.
“We know India’s position on the Ukrainian conflict, and to a great extent... it corresponds with our own position, because we do want the resolution of the Ukrainian conflict by peaceful means, and Russia is open to this process,” Peskov said.

He denied that Brics was considering de-dollarisation but said certain countries were using their national currencies as tools of political oppression and called the proposed US sanctions illegal and unacceptable.
Committing to further expanding energy cooperation with India, the official said India’s energy imports from Russia are at a record high. “I don’t want to give you any figures for understandable reasons, but every month we have a new record,” he said, briefing journalists virtually ahead of Putin’s visit.
The official also said that delivery of Russia’s S-400 Triumf air defence systems to India in 2026 was also on the agenda. “Russia is capable of fulfilling its obligations, and they will be fulfilled. This issue is being mentioned during the conversations of our two leaders,” said Peskov.

briefs.headline: VIT Chennai, The Hindu to hold conclave on the future of biotechnology on Sept. 11
briefs.deck: Higher secondary students, undergraduates, researchers, and biotechnology aspirants will have an opportunity to engage with experts and gain insights into emerging technologies, research pathways, careers, and the challenges confronting the sector
briefs.bodyText:
As biotechnology moves increasingly from the laboratory into everyday life, transforming healthcare, diagnostics, pharmaceuticals, and sustainability, the need to understand its possibilities and implications has never been greater.
Bringing together some of the country’s leading voices in science, research, healthcare, and industry, The Hindu and the Vellore Institute of Technology (VIT), Chennai will present the Biotech Conclave 2026 in Chennai on Friday (September 11, 2026).
The one-day conclave will be inaugurated by CII-president designate Dr. Suchitra Ella, the co-founder and MD of Bharat Biotech, who will deliver the inaugural address, and presided over by G. Viswanathan, founder and chancellor, VIT.
Higher secondary students, undergraduates, researchers, and biotechnology aspirants will have an opportunity to engage with experts and gain insights into emerging technologies, research pathways, careers, and the challenges confronting the sector.
The programme brings together a diverse group of eminent scientists, researchers, healthcare leaders and policymakers, including Professor K. VijayRaghavan, Dr. Vasan Sambandamurthy, Dr. Vinod Scaria, Dr. Ganapathy, Dr. Maneesh Paul, Dr. Kalpana Gowrishankar, Mayur Abhaya, and Ajay Mahipal, among others.
The sessions will examine the role of technology in accelerating biotechnology research, the possibilities offered by gene editing and precision medicine, India’s emergence as a global biopharma hub, the country’s research and innovation ecosystem, and the funding landscape for biotechnology research.
“Biotechnology represents one of the most consequential frontiers of education and research, with the power to improve lives and address some of society’s most urgent challenges. Through this conclave, VIT Chennai aims to encourage students to see biotechnology not only as a field of study, but as a pathway to innovation, enterprise, and meaningful service to humanity,” G. V. Selvam, vice-president, VIT, said.
“For The Hindu, this conclave is an opportunity to bring meaningful, accessible and forward-looking conversations on science to young audiences. By convening students, researchers, experts and industry voices on one platform, we hope to deepen public engagement with biotechnology and inspire informed curiosity about the field’s role in India’s future,” Sundar Kondur, chief revenue officer, The Hindu Group, said.

stories.headline: Karnataka high court tells trial court to pass fresh order in Darshan approver case
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: Citing procedural aberrations, the high court Tuesday set aside a trial court order granting conditional pardon to Pradosh, accused no. 14 in the Renukaswamy murder case who was granted the status of an approver.
Justice M Nagaprasanna passed the order after partly allowing the petition filed by actor 
Darshan

stories.headline: How peptide party led to raids on Amazon warehouses in Bengaluru
stories.bodyText:
Bengaluru
: A proposed peptide party promoted on social media eventually led Food Safety and Drug Administration (FDA) officials to 
Amazon
’s dark stores in Bengaluru and other warehouses, after the organisers allegedly told investigators that products linked to the event had been sourced from the e-commerce giant’s facilities.
The party, scheduled for Aug 29, was cancelled after the department served notices on the organisers and scrutinised the documents submitted by them. During verification, officials found that the organisers had allegedly attempted to source pharmaceutical and nutritional products through Amazon’s dark stores.
Health minister UT Khader said, “During the inquiry, officials found out that they tried to source pharma and nutrients from Amazon dark stores. Our officials then visited the facilities and found drugs worth more than Rs 4 lakh stored without a legal licence.”
At Amazon’s unit in Hitech Defence and Aerospace Park, Devanahalli, officials found food products carrying incorrect and inadequate labels that did not conform to prescribed food-safety standards. Food products worth around Rs 24 lakh were seized, while drugs worth Rs 2.5 lakh were found stored without the required licence, a FDA release stated.
A separate inspection at Amazon’s supply unit in Madivala and Thattananahalli village in Anekal taluk found food products worth around Rs 19 lakh with incorrect or inadequate labelling. Officials seized food products worth approximately Rs 32 lakh and also found drugs valued at over Rs 1.6 lakh stored without the necessary licence.
Amazon, however, is yet to react on the raids.

stories.headline: Bengaluru civic bodies collect half of annual property tax target, but weekly pace lags
stories.bodyText:
For the fiscal year 2026–2027, the five corporations under the Greater Bengaluru Authority (GBA) have a combined property tax revenue target of ₹6,700 crore, according to GBA data. By the end of August, the corporations had already collected ₹3,372.48 crore, which is 50.3% of the annual target.
Compared with the previous year’s collection for the same period, which stood at ₹3,211 crore, the corporations have achieved 5% higher revenue collection this year.
While there has been a minor increase, the new civic bodies are still struggling to maintain the required weekly pace, as they are able to achieve only 40% to 60% of the total weekly target, which is pegged at ₹103.99 crore.
According to the report, the city has 21,73,630 properties in the tax base, including residential, non-residential, mixed-use, and vacant properties. The actual revenue potential from these properties is pegged at ₹4,066.11 crore. The inclusion of arrears and revisions takes the target revenue to ₹6,700 crore.
Positive expansion, but not enough
The civic bodies have identified 3.19 lakh defaulters who owe the corporations ₹609.32 crore. In addition, the corporations have identified 32,215 cases under revision enforcement, which is expected to fetch ₹554 crore.
The figures indicate that the corporations are steadily expanding the property tax revenue base, even as they have failed to unlock new revenue avenues. Even last year, the final property tax collection was below ₹4,100 crore, leaving over ₹2,000 crore in arrears. However, the current trend indicates that tax collection is likely to cross the previous year’s figure.
Despite a good performance comparatively, enforcement needs to be tightened so that the corporations can significantly step up collections in the remaining months and stay on course to meet the annual target.
Positive about increase
A city corporation commissioner explained to The Hindu that the civic bodies are actively attempting to reach the target, as there is a high reliance on property tax to keep their revenue base healthy.
“During the civic budget, several works were planned, expecting revenue from avenues like the B-Khata conversion scheme and other sources. But many of those have not fetched the expected revenue, so we are trying our best to keep the available revenue streams healthy,” he explained.
The official further explained that despite a staff crunch due to several surveys, property tax collection has been better than last year. Once staff strength increases, the corporations are looking at tightening the collection and enforcement processes.
How the civic bodies fared
According to the data, the East Corporation has recorded the highest proportion of its target, collecting ₹882.22 crore, or 52.72%, of its target. West followed with ₹667.16 crore (52.06%), while South and Central have achieved 50.37% and 50.13%, respectively.
North has lagged behind the other corporations, collecting ₹565.56 crore, or 45.52%, of its ₹1,242.33-crore target. However, it has registered the highest year-on-year increase in collections at 9.15%.

stories.headline: Bengaluru South Corporation deploys AI cameras to track potholes, garbage dumping, and encroachments
stories.deck: The AI system is also intended to detect the misuse of building basements
stories.bodyText:
The Bengaluru South City Corporation has introduced an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based vehicle inspection system on a pilot basis to identify civic issues on roads, including footpath encroachments, potholes, garbage dumping, and construction debris.
K.N. Ramesh, South Corporation Commissioner, said the inspection vehicle, fitted with AI-enabled cameras and GPS devices, would capture photographs and videos while travelling along roads. “The system will analyse the visuals and identify and categorise civic issues, then it will automatically be forwarded to the officials concerned,” he said.
“Around 75 km of roads, out of the corporation’s total network of 311 roads, have been selected for the pilot project. If the system delivers the expected results, we plan to extend it across the jurisdiction,” Mr. Ramesh added.
Misuse of basements
The AI system is also intended to detect the misuse of building basements. It will identify cases where basements have been converted into commercial establishments, besides flagging unauthorised shops, advertising boards, and footpath encroachments. The corporation will also explore its use for property tax revision and detection of building bylaw violations.
Each issue detected during the survey will be automatically registered as a complaint ticket along with its GPS location. The tickets will be routed to the assistant executive engineer.
Before and after
Further, officials will have to inspect the reported locations and take action. Once the issue is resolved, the official will have to upload pictures showing the condition before and after, following which the ticket will be closed, according to Mr. Ramesh.

briefs.headline: And the vote goes to...: SIR woes of VIPs cleared at home in Bengaluru
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: Tens of VIPs in Bengaluru, including Kannada movie star Shivarajkumar who had received notices in the no-mapping category under special intensive revision of electoral rolls, didn’t have to go to GBA office with a clutch of documents to set right logical discrepancies. Instead, SIR officers carried out the verification exercise at their homes.
The VIP list which enjoyed this privilege included judges, MPs and MLAs, other senior politicians, bureaucrats, achievers in sports, cinema and other fields.
Pommala Sunil Kumar, additional district election officer, Bengaluru North, said: “We’ve a provision to complete the process for VIPs without their appearance at the hearing. The BLO concerned will complete the process at their doorstep,” Kumar said.
Sources said actor Shivarajkumar’s family had stayed at Manyata Tech Park and was registered to vote at a booth in Rachenahalli. Since his name did not figure in the 2002 SIR electoral roll, it could not be mapped to the earlier roll, and the system automatically generated a notice asking him to appear for a hearing.
Once officials identified the voter as the actor, they decided against issuing him a notice. 
Instead, they chose to collect the required documents and complete verification without his personal appearance.
Other VIPs, too, were asked not to come to the BBMP offices. BLOs processed their notices at their homes.
Voters facing health issues  also skip office visitBengaluru: Not just VIPs, even voters with age or health issues were able to complete the process at home as BLOs and AEROs visited them for the verification exercise.
Booth-level officer Faiza Begum of RK Hegde Nagar in north Bengaluru went to the residence of an 82-year-old voter at Bharatiya City on Tuesday to complete the hearing process.
In another case, AERO MB Prakash and his team walked out to a car parked outside a community hall in RK Hegde Nagar, where an accident victim unable to walk was waiting.
“A 35-year-old woman had suffered a fracture in an accident recently. She came to the hearing venue in a car, and when the staff learnt that she could not walk, they went to her vehicle and completed the hearing process,” an officer said.
Most voters who turned up for SIR hearings in Bengaluru said they were satisfied with how officials handled the process and the arrangements at the venues. Officials said a majority who received notices produced valid documents for verification, while only a few could not — in those cases, staff considered their claims based on declaration forms issued by BLOs.

briefs.headline: Beards, blazer and a campus protest: Dress code sparks stir in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Management denies: says they were only asked to come in uniform
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: A college dress code became the unlikely trigger for a student protest in the city Monday, after a group of students of Indian Academy Degree College alleged they were asked to leave the campus for not wearing the prescribed uniform and for having beards.
A group of students of the college, in Hennur Cross, alleged that the management asked them to come in uniform and be clean-shaven and get haircuts. When they refused, the authorities allegedly asked them to leave the campus. As the number of students sent off campus increased, they soon united and turned it into a demonstration.
As the crowd began to build up on the main road, police also stepped in, fearing traffic disruption. “Monday afternoon, we received a message that some students had come to the road and were protesting. Worried they might block the road, we arrived at the spot. The issue was that many students were not wearing the regular uniform. They had beards, some untrimmed, some with cut lines. We had a discussion and asked them to wear uniform and come dressed decently,” said a police officer.
However, the college denied that the students were asked to shave off their beards. 
“The issue was with dress code compliance. Monday is a uniform day when students have to wear a blazer, tie and shirt. Many of them did not come in uniform. The teachers asked them to go change and come. With this, the students went out and formed a crowd. Police also came in and asked the students to follow the college rules,” said principal Bharathi. “We have told them (students) to be well-groomed. We have a dress code which insists on a proper haircut and well-trimmed beard,” she added.
Some students took to social media to express their resentment. “Students wanted a simple explanation. Why are these rules compulsory? Why should students have no choice regarding their appearance? And why weren’t students’ concerns heard properly? Students were sent outside the college gate and made to stand on the main road while the situation continued. This raised an even bigger question: why were students protesting about college rules being pushed outside instead of being heard inside?” read one social media post. “Students raising genuine concerns should not automatically be treated as troublemakers. A college is not just a place where students follow instructions. It is a place where students learn to think, question, discuss and speak up.”

briefs.headline: 2.1 lakh Karnataka students to spend night on farms, to experience village life firsthand
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: To understand — and appreciate — that ‘India lives in its villages’ as the Mahatma declared, Karnataka govt is sending 2.1 lakh students from 931 urban schools and pre-university institutions to villages this academic year to experience rural life, agriculture and the realities of farming.
The destination of the next school trip may not be a museum, science centre or amusement park. Rather, it’ll be villages, the soul of India. Or, Bharat. Under ‘Gramanubhava’ (Rural Experience), students will spend one night and two days in rural areas between Sept and Dec 2026, swapping classroom lessons for fields, farms and interactions with farming families.
Approved through a govt order on Sept 7 as part of the state cabinet’s ‘First 100 Days’ agenda, the Rs 13-crore programme aims to narrow the urban-rural divide by making the countryside a classroom.
Students will spend 6-8 hours in structured interaction with farmers. Depending on the location, they will get hands-on exposure to agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry and farm practices, apart from learning about composting, organic waste management, seed selection, soil health, water conservation and farm equipment. The experience will extend beyond the farm gate. Students will visit farmer producer organisations, self-help groups and demonstration units to understand what happens after crops leave the field — including sorting, packaging, processing and marketing.
Besides, students will explore local art, traditional crafts, heritage and indigenous knowledge systems, while maintaining journals and worksheets recording what they see and learn.
Villages less than 50km from school
Govt has fixed Rs 25,000 for a batch of 50 students and five accompanying teachers for the farm trip. Of this, Rs 16,000 will go towards transport, Rs 5,000 towards food and refreshments, Rs 2,000 as an honorarium or memento for the host farmer, and Rs 2,000 towards contingencies.
Students will travel in state transport vehicles. Farms and learning centres will have to be inspected and certified as safe by officials from the agriculture and school education departments before students are taken there. To keep travel manageable, learning centres have been advised to be located within 50km from schools. Parental consent is mandatory. School heads and accompanying teachers will be responsible for student safety throughout the visit.
Students to present project work
Between Jan and Feb 2027, students will turn observations into projects, preparing models, developing school nutrition gardens and organising presentations and exhibitions based on their experiences.
Likely takeaways
* Dialogue with farmers to study crop selection, seasonal management, food production, rural livelihoods & systemic challenges
* Field observation of agriculture, horticulture, dairy farming, sericulture, poultry farming, agro-forestry & related rural allied enterprises
* Exposure to soil health testing, composting, organic manure preparation, seed selection, water harvesting, nutrition/kitchen gardens, modern farming machinery & sustainable agriculture
* Understanding the agribusiness value chain, including post-harvest storage, grading, processing, packaging, FPO logistics & primary/secondary market distribution channels
* Mandatory entry of daily learning, observations, and individual reflections in worksheets and field-learning diaries during the residency

briefs.headline: 19 minors rescued from Yeshwantpur APMC market in Bengaluru after CM’s visit
briefs.bodyText:
Bengaluru: City police rescued 19 minors, including one girl, from shops and loading-unloading points at Yeshwantpur APMC market Tuesday, within hours of chief minister DK Shivakumar spotting child labourers there.
During a surprise visit around 6am, Shivakumar spotted children working at the market and directed officials to act against both those employing them and those sending them to work.
Soon, police formed five special teams, led by DCP (North) Babasab Nemagoud, and searched the market. Four shopowners were arrested. City police commissioner Seemanth Kumar Singh said cases were registered against Shahid Majid, 60, B Prakash, 39, Amir S, 33, and Mohammed Saif, 27, under the Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act and the Child and Adolescent Labour (Prohibition and Regulation) Act, 1986.
“Some individuals drew the CM’s attention to children being made to work in different shops and at loading and unloading points. In less than two hours, the police teams rescued 19 children,” Singh said.
Shivakumar also ordered the dismissal of a cooperative society secretary after learning that the crop insurance claims of 93 farmers in Devara Hipparagi taluk had been rejected, allegedly because their premiums were not deposited with DCC Bank. 
A farmer told Shivakumar that the farmers had paid the premiums to the society but later received messages saying their claims had been rejected. After checking the list of farmers who had made payments, the CM directed officials to act against the secretary.
At the APMC market, Shivakumar heard complaints from farmers, traders and mandi owners about police harassment, delayed payments, commissions, cultivation costs, and weighing practices. He also checked the weighing of onions.
Farmers said markets in Kalaburagi, Bidar, and Vijayapura charged commissions of Rs 8 to Rs 10, while no commission was collected at Yeshwantpur, making it preferable for farmers. They also said deficient rainfall had reduced onion yields from the usual 150 to 200 bags an acre to around 50 bags this year. Excessive rain could cause the crop to rot, while low prices could make it difficult to recover transportation costs.
Shivakumar warned traders against collecting excess charges and directed officials to prevent manipulation of weighing scales. He also asked farmers to report violations.
Anjunappa, an onion farmer from Hosahatti village in Kudligi, told the CM that he had built a house on his farmland but had not received power connection despite applying for one. Several other households faced a similar problem, he said. Shivakumar directed officials to collect details and provide connections to the affected households. He also asked farmers to raise such grievances during the govt’s Prajaseva programmes.

briefs.headline: Expired, mislabelled food products worth ₹1.38 crore and medicines worth ₹4.02 lakh seized in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Among other places, a Swiggy Instamart unit at Hosakote in Bengaluru Rural was closed after expired items worth ₹42 lakh were seized from the unit
briefs.bodyText:
Officials of the Food Safety and Drug Administration (FSDA) department have seized expired and improperly labelled food products, including chocolates, biscuits, and dry fruits, worth ₹1.38 crore and also medicines worth ₹4.02 lakh that were procured without licences.
Addressing mediapersons on September 8 in Bengaluru, Minister for Health and Family Welfare U.T. Khader said, ”The inspection began when I received a message from a media representative about a peptide party happening at Koramangala in Bengaluru. While the party was cancelled, I instructed the officials to track and check the supply chain of items provided in this kind of party.
“When we enquired with the organisers about the concept of peptide party, they said it is about introducing new pharma medicines and nutrition-based food to elite class people. On asking more about the supply chain of pharmaceutical products, it was found that they are sourcing it from the dark stores of Amazon located in and around Bengaluru.”
The Minister informed that the department raided two such stores in Anekal and Devanahalli.
Food products and medicines seized
“On tracking the supply chain further, officials learnt about Leo 7 Enterprises unit at Lingarajpuram. They found expired food items worth ₹45 lakh, which was seized. The owner of Leo 7 Enterprises procured expired items from different places, and sold them in such parties and other places. It will take another three days to inspect the entire premises. We have shut down the unit,” he said.
Revealing further details about the raid, the Minister said, “An inspection of the Leo 7 Enterprises unit revealed various expired and near-expiry food items, including nutritional products, beverages, chocolates, sweets, ghee, and nuts/seeds. According to the information provided by the owner of the unit, food items worth about ₹1,56 lakh were stored in the unit.”
Similarly, a Swiggy Instamart unit at Hosakote in Bengaluru Rural was closed after expired items worth ₹42 lakh were seized from the unit. As per the details shared by the department, the unit was closed due to unhygienic conditions and violation of the Food Safety and Standards Act. Further legal action is being taken under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006 and applicable FSSAI Regulations. An inspection is pending. Expired and mislabelled products worth about ₹1 crore have been found, the Minister informed.
During the inspection, compliance with mandatory labeling, manufacturing date, expiry date, shelf life and other food safety standards of food products sold through online and e-commerce platforms was checked.
At the same time, officials came across procurement of medicines without a licence. All these items were seized from various units in Anekal, Devanahalli and other places.
Meanwhile, at Amazon Hitech Defence and Aerospace Park in Devanahalli, food products worth ₹14 lakhs with incorrect and inadequate labelling were seized. Expired food products worth ₹6 lakh were seized. The total value of food products seized from this unit is ₹20 lakh. Officials have also seized medicines worth ₹2,45,352, which were procured without a licence.
Officials inspected Amazon stores in Thattanahalli village near Anekal taluk, and seized food products worth ₹19 lakh. According to the officials, these products were incorrectly labelled. Expired food products worth ₹13 lakh were also seized. The total value of food products seized from this unit is ₹32 lakh. Meanwhile, medicines worth ₹1,57,000, which were procured without a licence, were seized.
A food business located at Sapta Bazaar in HBR Layout in Bengaluru was inspected after it was found that groceries, milk, vegetables, yogurt and other food items that were being purchased from various e-commerce companies, and expired food products were being resold to consumers. Various expired food products, including cashew biscuits, Vijay Ragi Flour, chicken patty, paneer, cookies, nuts, eggs, and flour worth ₹10,000 were seized.

briefs.headline: SIR: Notices cite errors despite correct details in forms; hearing to begin from Sept. 5 in Bengaluru
briefs.deck: Once the process of generating a notice is initiated, it takes a week before a hearing can be held, with the first hearing possible only on the seventh day
briefs.bodyText:
While the disposal of notices in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls was supposed to begin on August 24 across Karnataka as per the ECI’s guidelines, Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) in Bengaluru said they generated the notices only on August 28.
Once the process of generating a notice is initiated, it takes a week before a hearing can be held, with the first hearing possible only on the seventh day. In Bengaluru, therefore, hearings can begin only on September 5 — meaning 10 days have already been lost in a process that is already working against a tight deadline.
Also Read: SIR: Notice hearing at 12 a.m., only Kannada notices and inaccessible BLOs leave voters struggling
Huge workload
The hearings will continue until October 22, leaving EROs less than 60 days to conclude cases involving 43.81 lakh voters across Karnataka. Over 24 lakh of these cases are concentrated in Bengaluru alone.
The tight timeline is also expected to create difficulties for voters in receiving the notices and preparing documents for the hearings. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) said they received the notices only on September 1, while distribution began on Wednesday. Given the volume of notices, they said distribution, in many cases, could continue until September 4 — just a day before the hearings begin. “Some people may get enough time, like at least two days, but some may not even get a day. While September 5 was decided as it is a Saturday to cause less inconvenience to the public, this cannot be done each time,” a BLO said.
Notices
There are also questions over the reasons cited in some of the notices. Karnataka Chief Electoral Officer V. Anbu Kumar, referring to the total number of notices, had said they would be served to voters with logical discrepancies or those whose details, or those of their family members, could not be mapped to the 2002 rolls. However, in several cases, voters who said they had provided the required details in their enumeration forms have also received notices, with the reasons cited not matching the details they had submitted.
For instance, in a notice accessed by The Hindu, a 71-year-old man from the Raichur constituency was issued a notice citing two reasons — that “the age gap between you and another progeny linked with the same parent is less than nine months” and that “the age difference between you and your parent, whose details are used to link you with the rolls prepared during the last SIR, is less than 15 years, that seems to be due to incorrect matching”.
However, the elector’s first son is 40 years old — born on June 1, 1984, while another son was born on August 26, 1985 — a gap of more than 13 months. Moreover, if the elector’s son is the person whose age creates that discrepancy, then the son should logically be the elector flagged for that particular discrepancy, not the father.
In another case in C.V. Raman Nagar, a voter and her mother were informed about the notices over the call, stating that they had not provided details for mapping. However, when checked, both their enumeration forms contained mapping details. In this case, voters were told that notice will be served, but it was yet not delivered, with electors not even knowing the hearing date.
The confusion seen during the enumeration phase, when several voters received calls asking them to collect enumeration forms and were unsure whether documents had to be submitted, also appears to have persisted into the notice process. Several voters said that BLOs had collected documents from them, saying this would “fasten the process” or “reduce discrepancies”. Some said they had received calls on Wednesday asking them to come to the polling station to collect their notices if they wanted them “on time”.
In many other cases, voters said BLOs had already collected documents, including caste certificates, Aadhaar cards, Class 10 certificates and transfer certificates. The voters, however, said they were unclear about why the documents were being collected or whether they were even required to submit them at this stage.
As per the guidelines, BLOs cannot collect any documents. Documents can be sought during the hearing process.

stories.headline: Copper hits all-time high, Brent nears century mark
stories.deck: Crude Shock: Indian Basket Trades Above $100 Per Barrel
stories.bodyText:
MUMBAI: Copper and crude oil, two important industrial raw materials for several industries, are on a tear. According to notes from Vedanta and ICICI Securities, a combination of factors like tightening mine supply, especially from Chile, shifting global trade flows amid potential US tariffs on refined copper, and accelerating demand from electrification, renewable energy, power infrastructure and AI are behind the recent rally in copper prices.
For crude prices, the rally is mainly on the back of rising geopolitical tensions in the Persian Gulf region, one of the major sources of crude oil and gas globally.
Coming at a time when the economy is facing a sluggish demand environment, the rise in prices of these commodities is raising fears that several companies may have to either go for a price hike or absorb higher costs, squeezing profit margins. If crude prices sustain near or above the $100 mark, that could also add to the inflationary pressure, raising chances of a rate hike by RBI.
On Tuesday, on London Metal Exchange (LME), copper three-month futures hit a high of $14,617/tonne, an all-time high. And in the international markets, Brent crude inched closer to the $100/barrel mark while the Indian crude basket, the biggest import item for the country in terms of value, went past the $100 mark early this month.
The rally in prices of these commodities is also attracting investors to buy stocks of companies that are going to benefit from higher prices. 
On BSE on Tuesday, among the copper miners and producers, Hindustan Copper closed about 4.7% higher, Vedanta closed 1.3% up while Onix Solar, MSCTC and Bhagyanagar India, all three stocks, closed 5% up. Among the oil stocks, while Oil India closed 2.1%, ONGC closed 1% up.
While the rally in copper is positive for Indian producers and miners of the metal, this could, on the other hand, increase input costs for sectors like real estate, cables & wires, electrical & electronic equipment, and power production, transmission & distribution.
A report by real estate consultancy firm Anarock Property Consultants noted that due to the war in West Asia, mechanical, electrical & plumbing (MEP) costs in the real estate sector have risen by 8-12%, part of which is attributed to the rising prices of copper. In the last one year, the price of the metal has risen about 17%.

stories.headline: Digital asset firms court sovereign funds
stories.bodyText:

Brics summit

stories.headline: Reliance plans first local debt sale after three years with $1.32 billion fundraise, bankers say
stories.deck: The oil-to-telecom conglomerate plans to raise 125 billion rupees ($1.32 ‌billion) through a sale of five-year notes, at an annual coupon of 7.47%, ‌and is set to invite bids from ‌investors in ⁠the week ending September 18, ⁠according to bankers.
stories.bodyText:
Billionaire Mukesh Ambani’s Reliance Industries is set to return to India’s rupee bond market after nearly three years, five merchant bankers told Reuters late on Monday (September 8, 2026), with what would be the largest single-tranche fundraising by a rated firm since November 2023.
The oil-to-telecom conglomerate plans to raise 125 billion rupees ($1.32 billion) through a sale of five-year notes, at an annual coupon of 7.47%, and is set to invite bids from investors in the week ending September 18, according to bankers.
The issue would be RIL’s first rupee bond offering since November 2023, when it raised 200 billion rupees in what was the largest local-currency debt sale by an Indian non-financial company.
The bankers requested anonymity as they are not authorised to speak to the media, while the company did not immediately reply to a Reuters email seeking comment outside normal business hours.
A sharp decline in yields on up to five-year bonds locally has made such funding cheaper than dollar debt sales, the bankers added.
The five-year government bond yield has plunged 33 basis points since the start of June, mainly backed by mammoth dollar inflows under the central bank’s subsidised schemes.
Flows led by those in the non-resident dollar deposit scheme pulled down local yields, while higher U.S. Treasury rates lifted the cost of dollar funding for Indian borrowers.
Large private banks are acting as arrangers for the deal, and are also set to partly subscribe to these bonds, the bankers added.

briefs.headline: ONGC Chairman calls for greater focus on tech, innovation; commits to fund and support startups
briefs.deck: Stating that India must become more efficient and innovative to address its energy requirements, he said there was a need to do things “fundamentally different” to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imports
briefs.bodyText:
India needs to prioritise its resources towards technologies that address the country’s immediate and strategic energy requirements, said Arun Kumar Singh, Chairman & CEO, Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC), on Tuesday (September 8, 2026), while calling for a greater focus on technology, innovation and efficient deployment of resources to strengthen India’s energy security.
He was speaking at the MC²+ IGNITE Mumbai City Connect at IIT Bombay, which was organised by ONGC in association with MC²+ Ignite to identify start-ups which would be funded to undertake innovations in specified areas of the core energy sector.
Stating that India must become more efficient and innovative to address its energy requirements, he said there was a need to do things “fundamentally different” to strengthen energy security and reduce dependence on imports.
Highlighting the importance of innovation in areas that have a direct bearing on the country’s energy needs, he emphasised the need for a more focused approach to innovation and technology development.
Mr. Singh said artificial intelligence would help to improve production efficiency, reduce wastage and make assets and processes more efficient. He also pointed to the potential of AI in areas such as enhanced oil recovery and exploration.
He also emphasised that India needs to strike a balance between pursuing futuristic technologies and addressing immediate national priorities. With resources being limited, he said the country needs to learn to “prioritise our resources on where we should spend”.
MC²+ IGNITE, which has been set up under the initiative of the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, will support up to 30 high-potential early-stage start-ups. The programme offers a ₹30 crore grant pooled from public sector oil & gas companies and up to ₹2 crore in milestone-linked convertible funding for selected start-ups. It covers six deep-tech energy themes and an Open Theme, with opportunities for access to real pilot sites, infrastructure and laboratory facilities, technical mentorship, industry access and pathways for pilot deployment and procurement.
On Tuesday (September 8), a tripartite MoU was signed between MC²+ Foundation, IIT Bombay and IIT Bombay’s Society for Innovation and Entrepreneurship (SINE), to strengthen collaboration between industry, academia and the start-up ecosystem.
As a partner PSU in the MC²+ ecosystem, ONGC will collaborate across AI-driven Subsurface Intelligence and the other energy innovation themes, helping start-ups access R&D facilities, mentorship, funding, market opportunities and pilot projects.
MC²+ is an energy innovation platform which seeks to strengthen India’s energy innovation ecosystem by supporting promising start-ups and technologies through funding, mentorship, infrastructure and industry access.
The Mumbai City Connect event brought together senior leaders from industry and academia, entrepreneurs and the deep-tech ecosystem.
Participants included Prof. Aniruddha B. Pandit, Vice Chancellor, Institute of Chemical Technology, Mumbai; Prof. Shireesh Kedare, Director, IIT Bombay; Dhananjay Rai, representing MC²+; Shaji Varghese, CEO, SINE; Prof. Nishant Sharma, SINE; Prof. Yogendra Shastri, CoEOGE and senior ONGC officials.

briefs.headline: Seven applications received for coal gasification package: Government
briefs.deck: The Union Cabinet on May 13 approved a ₹37,500 crore package aimed at promoting surface coal and lignite gasification in the country
briefs.bodyText:
The Coal Ministry informed Tuesday that it has received seven applications seeking the financial support for setting up of coal gasification projects in the country.
In a statement, the ministry elaborated that it received three applications from Adani Enterprises for setting up coal-to-urea gasification plants, one from Shyam Sel & Power Limited for producing syngas, one from Gallantt Ispat Ltd for direct reduced iron and syngas.
It had earlier informed that NTPC Ltd and Talcher Fertilisers (TFL) too had put forth applications. The state-owned power distributor is seeking to produce synthetic natural gas whilst TFL too has applied for a urea gasification plant.
The applications would now be evaluated in accordance with guidelines of the scheme.
Further, with the conclusion of the first round, the second round of the rolling window for applications commenced Sept 8.
G. Kishan Reddy, Union Minister for Coal and Mines termed the now-concluded window as a success.
Speaking to the press, he said, “The second window [of the rolling application system] commences today. A good number of companies applied in the first phase, and we expect that more companies would turn in the second phase.”
The Coal Ministry had stated earlier in the day that several prospective applicants were presently at “advanced stages of project preparation” to submit proposals in subsequent windows.
According to Atanu Mukherjee, CEO at the energy engineering and advisory company Dastur Energy, carving sustainable project economics would essay an important role in the next phase.
He underlined that gasification projects, are capital intensive, and their bankability depends on technology suited to Indian coal, scale, long-term product offtake and competitive financing, among other things.
“The government’s incentive framework can help absorb some of the early-stage risk, but ultimately these projects will have to demonstrate sustainable returns without being permanently dependent on subsidy,” he said.
The Union Cabinet had on May 13 approved a ₹37,500 crore package aimed at promoting surface coal and lignite gasification in the country. The request for proposal (RfP) was subsequently issued, with the current application window closing on September 7.
India has a target of gasifying 100 million tonnes (MT) of coal by 2030.
The May 13 package builds further on an earlier ₹8,500 crore package that saw eight projects being given a nod which are presently at varied stages of implementation. Talcher Fertiliser’s coal-based ammonia and urea complex would be the first of them – scheduled for commissioning in fiscal year 2027-28.

briefs.headline: NDR Group proposes public listing of NDR InvIT Trust, files for ₹750-crore IPO

briefs.bodyText:
NDR Group has proposed to take its warehousing and industrial infrastructure platform public, with NDR InvIT Trust filing a draft offer document for a ₹750-crore public issue.

briefs.headline: Public Accounts Committee flags failure to transfer ₹9,222 crore in cess collections to designated reserve funds
briefs.deck: Members question the Finance Ministry’s explanation; panel chief K.C. Venugopal says cess proceeds must not be used to finance fiscal deficit instead of their intended purpose
briefs.bodyText:
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) on Tuesday (September 8, 2026) expressed concern over the reported failure to transfer cess and levy collections to designated reserve funds, with members questioning the Union Finance Ministry’s explanation on the issue and reiterating earlier recommendations that such collections be used only for the purposes for which they were raised.
According to an audit examination for 2024-25, ₹9,222 crore collected through various cesses and levies was not transferred to four designated reserve funds during the year. The findings form part of Paragraph 3.3.1 of the Comptroller and Auditor General’s (CAG’s) Report No. 6 of 2026.
According to sources, PAC chairperson and senior Congress leader K.C. Venugopal said the issue had already been flagged by the committee in its 69th Report, tabled in August 2023. The report had recommended scientific assessments of the amount and duration of cess collections, periodic reviews to evaluate whether intended objectives had been achieved, and regular crediting of cess proceeds to reserve funds. Ignoring the directions of the PAC, which is a parliamentary standing committee, constitutes an insult to Parliament, Mr. Venugopal said.
‘Collected from everyone’
He further argued that cess collections should be utilised for the purposes for which they are raised and not to finance the government’s budgetary deficit. He also noted that cess collections are not part of the divisible pool of taxes and are therefore not shared with States. This, he said, makes the problem further acute since the Central government must utilise this amount to renew the facilities available to citizens. It is an amount collected from everyone, whether they are income tax payees or not, from the middle-class to the poor, Mr. Venugopal pointed out.
Reserve funds are constituted for specific purposes under statutory provisions or executive orders and are financed through budgetary support, grants, contributions, cesses and levies collected in the Consolidated Fund of India.
In 2024-25, the Union government collected ₹3,89,220 crore through cesses, charges and levies, accounting for 10.25% of its gross tax revenue. The CAG found that the largest shortfall that year was linked to the Pradhan Mantri Swasthya Suraksha Nidhi (PMSSN), where only ₹14,439 crore was transferred against collections of ₹21,085 crore, leaving a gap of ₹6,646 crore.
The audit also flagged the Oil Industry Development Fund (OIDF). While cumulative collections through the oil industry cess since 1974-75 amounted to ₹3,12,782 crore, only ₹902 crore was transferred to the Oil Industry Development Board up to 1991-92 and none thereafter until 2023-24. Though the OIDF was operationalised for the first time in 2024-25, auditors found a short transfer of ₹201 crore. As of March 31, 2025, ₹2,94,150 crore remained in the Consolidated Fund of India.
The audit further noted that 10 reserve funds and 21 deposit accounts with aggregate credit balances of ₹844.93 crore had remained dormant for three or more financial years.
Finance Ministry’s argument
The Finance Ministry has contested some of the audit findings, arguing that the assessment of Health and Education Cess transfers excluded the Madhyamik and Uchchtar Shiksha Kosh (MUSK). It said that against collections of ₹84,339 crore in 2024-25, transfers to the three designated funds totalled ₹86,020 crore, resulting in a net excess transfer of ₹1,681 crore. According to the Ministry, the higher allocation to MUSK offset the PMSSN shortfall.
The Ministry also said that allocations made in the Revised Estimates for 2025-26 would address earlier shortfalls. It further argued that maintaining large idle balances in reserve funds was fiscally imprudent at a time when the government had borrowed about ₹15.74 lakh crore in 2024-25 to finance expenditure of ₹46.53 lakh crore, adding that such balances increased government liabilities.

briefs.headline: India has 51 days coal stocks to meet power demand; production recovers after monsoon disruption
briefs.deck: The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) had observed recently that 53 thermal power-plants were holding 25% or less than their overall coal requirements.
briefs.bodyText:
India has sufficient coal stocks to meet around 51 days of domestic power demand, Union Coal and Mines Minister G. Kishan Reddy said, allaying concerns over supply disruptions caused by heavy monsoon rains in coal-producing regions.
The country currently holds around 123.7 million tonnes (MT) of coal, including 23.7 MT stocked at thermal power plants, Reddy told reporters. With the power sector consuming nearly 2.4 MT of coal a day, the available stock is adequate to meet demand for about 51 days, he told in response to a query from The Hindu.
Reddy’s comments came amid concerns over coal inventories at thermal power plants. The Central Electricity Authority had recently observed that 53 thermal power plants were holding 25% or less of their required coal stock.
Coal production was affected for around 10 days due to monsoon rains in key coal-bearing regions, Reddy said. However, rainfall has eased over the past few days, allowing production to recover.
“We are monitoring the situation daily. Rainfall has eased in the last couple of days, thus production has increased. There is no need to worry about coal stocks,” Reddy said.
He added that if rainfall remains moderate for another week, coal production could increase further.
The Coal Ministry is also coordinating with coal-producing companies, the Ministries of Power and Railways to ensure adequate coal availability and smooth offtake, Reddy said.
Meanwhile, coal-based power generation rose 9.1% year-on-year to 535.8 billion units (BU) between April and August, according to government officials. “This was mainly due to El Niño conditions, coupled with an 11% decline in hydropower generation,” they explained.
Coal India’s production has also picked up sharply. According to the latest government data, the company’s average daily output increased by around 35% from the first three days of September to about 1.83 MT on September 6, indicating a recovery in production following the monsoon-related disruption.
