briefs.headline: Textile mills, garment units seek measures to improve cotton availability
briefs.bodyText:
E
With cotton and yarn prices continuing to fluctuate, textile mills and garment units in Tamil Nadu are seeking measures to improve cotton productivity and availability.
Spurt in demand for cotton yarn globally is among the main reasons for volatility in its prices, said Ashwin Chandran, chairman of the Confederation of Indian Textile Industry.
International demand for yarn is better than the last couple of years. Demand for cotton yarn was muted since 2023-24. Demand for textile products across the value chain started picking up last December. Most of the textile units maintained hand-to-mouth stocks for the last years because of the low demand.
Demand for yarn from China and Bangladesh saw an increase and domestic demand for garments is also seeing growth. This has led to better market for yarn. Further, hosiery yarn exports are mainly by the mills in Gujarat and not much from those in Tamil Nadu.
However, the cotton futures market went up to 92 cents for a pound and has corrected now to about 86 cents. Thus, the prices of cotton, the basic raw material, saw prices fluctuating. While the landed prices of clean cotton has seen ₹70 increase, yarn prices have increased by about ₹95 a kg in the last one year, he said.
The focus of the entire industry should be on improving cotton productivity in the country for raw material security, he added.
Meanwhile, the Tiruppur Exporters and Manufacturers Association has urged the Central and State governments to ban cotton exports. It said the State, especially the western districts, design and manufactures a wide range of textile products and supply to both, domestic and international markets.
This industry, predominantly driven by small and medium-sized enterprises, provides employment and livelihoods to thousands of people. However, since January this year, certain large spinning mills and traders “have been artificially restricting the supply of cotton, causing yarn prices to skyrocket and creating an unprecedented crisis for local manufacturing units—particularly the small and medium-sized ones,” alleged the Association.
Last year, cotton requirement was 350 lakh bales, whereas current domestic production stands at 290 lakh bales. With the existing cotton shortage, the government removed the import duty (11%) on cotton and 62 lakh bales of cotton were imported. Yet, cotton prices continue to rise.
This is due to artificial market manipulation, the Association claimed. The continuous rise in cotton prices have increased raw material costs, causing garment orders to be diverted to other States and countries, it said.

briefs.headline: Husband died in 2006, widow got PF and gratuity; why HC rejected pension claim
briefs.deck: On April 27, 2010, Bank of Maharashtra introduced a one-time option allowing a specified category of serving employees, retired employees and families of deceased employees to join the Pension Scheme, subject to the prescribed terms and conditions.
briefs.bodyText:
Her husband passed away in 2006 and she was not eligible for family pension. However, the bank her husband worked at opened a one-time pension eligibility window some years later which the widow applied for after the last date. A 
Delhi High Court
 has now rejected the widow’s pension claim. Here’s what the case is about:
Mr Ramesh Chand had been working with Bank of Maharashtra since March 1, 1985, and he died on February 12, 2006 when he was still in service. He was survived by his wife, Savitri Devi, and a son. Chand was covered under the contributory provident fund regime at the time of his death. The bank paid his terminal benefits, including provident fund and gratuity, to Devi on July 24, 2006.
Although Devi was not eligible for family pension under the existing arrangement at the time, her son was employed with the same bank.
On April 27, 2010, Bank of Maharashtra introduced a one-time option allowing a specified category of serving employees, retired employees and families of deceased employees to join the Pension Scheme, subject to the prescribed terms and conditions.
The bank subsequently set out the eligibility requirements through a circular issued on August 18, 2010. 
The circular covered the families of employees who had joined the bank before September 29, 1995, but died while still in service after that date.
On the face of it, Devi appeared to fall within this category. Her husband had joined the bank in 1985 and died while in service in 2006. So why was her pension claim rejected?
Why bank rejected widow’s pension claim
The bank opened the window for pension but eligibility by itself did not mean that the pension would be granted. Those who were covered by the scheme were required to exercise the option within the time limit and comply with the procedure laid down in the circular.
The deadline for submitting the application was October 18, 2010. The bank's circular made it clear that employees, retired employees and families of deceased employees whose forms did not reach the concerned branch or office within the prescribed period would not be eligible for pension or family pension.
Devi, however, submitted her application at Bank of Maharashtra's Connaught Place branch on March 2, 2011, several months after the deadline had passed.
Devi stated that she was willing to repay the bank's contribution to the Provident Fund, along with interest and the additional amount required under the scheme.
She followed this up with a handwritten letter to the bank on December 30, 2013, reiterating her position. According to her case, she received no response.
Devi then filed an RTI application to find out what had happened to her request. The information she received showed that the branch manager had contacted the bank's head office seeking guidance on her case. However, for reasons that remained unexplained, the branch did not forward Devi's application to the head office.
The RTI response also revealed that the bank's head office had instructed the branch to collect the required documents from Devi and send the complete set of papers back for consideration on merits. Nothing further came of the matter, however, and the reason for the lack of action remained unclear.
Devi argued that these records established that the bank was aware of her claim for family pension and therefore could not subsequently reject it on the ground that documents were missing or had not been submitted.
She eventually approached the court over the issue. The Delhi High Court, however, dismissed her case on July 7, 2026.
Why Delhi High Court rejected the widow’s pension claim
Shashwat Anand, Advocate on Record, Supreme Court of India, told ET that the Delhi High Court found the August 18, 2010 circular to be a one-time opportunity with a clearly defined deadline for opting into the Pension Scheme.
The last date for exercising the option was October 18, 2010. Devi, however, submitted her application only on March 2, 2011. There was also no contemporaneous receipt, date-stamp or acknowledgment from the branch to establish when her application had been received.
Anand said timely submission was not merely a procedural requirement but formed part of the conditions for acquiring the right under the pension scheme. As a result, equitable considerations could not be used to alter the pension scheme or set aside its mandatory eligibility requirements.
The lawyer also pointed out that the bank's internal correspondence from January 2014 was treated by the Delhi High Court as an administrative exchange. Itrelated to checking records and seeking instructions from the Head Office. The correspondence, therefore, could not be treated as an admission that the bank had received and accepted a valid option from Devi or had agreed to condone the delay.
The biggest point that went against Devi’s case was that she could not establish that the branch had received her application.
Devi maintained that she had submitted the pension option form on March 2, 2011. However, she could not produce evidence establishing that the branch had actually received it on that date. More importantly, the prescribed deadline under the circular was October 18, 2010.
There was no bank acknowledgment confirming receipt of the form at the Connaught Place branch on March 2, 2011. The circular itself required the family member to retain an acknowledged copy of the application. Devi did not produce any such copy bearing the branch's receipt or date-stamp before the High Court.
The Court consequently relied on the express terms of the pension scheme, which required applications to be submitted within the stipulated deadline and stated that forms received after that date would not be considered.
Since Devi had not demonstrated compliance with this requirement, the Court held that the delay could not give rise to an enforceable right to family pension.
The High Court also made it clear that equitable considerations could not be relied upon to create an entitlement de hors (outside) the Scheme.
The Delhi High Court also examined the bank's internal communication dated January 18, 2014. It held that the communication could not be interpreted as an unequivocal acknowledgment that Devi had submitted a valid option in March 2011 and that the bank was consequently required to act on it.
The communication had been issued after Devi claimed that she had submitted the option form but had not received any subsequent response from the bank.
When the branch forwarded a copy of the option form to the Head Office, it also recorded that a search of its records had failed to locate any document showing that the form had previously been sent to the Head Office.
The Delhi High Court said the communication in question did not establish the truth of Devi's claim.
The Delhi High Court acknowledged that the bank's handling of Devi's case showed some administrative laxity and indecision.
The Delhi High Court said: “However, such administrative shortcomings, howsoever regrettable, cannot operate to create or enlarge an entitlement that is otherwise unavailable under the governing circular.”
The Court made it clear that the legal basis for a family pension claim has to come from the applicable pension scheme itself. Procedural lapses in implementing that scheme cannot, by themselves, create such a right.
The Court therefore held that internal correspondence or a request to submit additional documents could not be treated as a final decision granting Devi a substantive entitlement to family pension.
The Delhi High Court recognised that family pension is a beneficial, welfare-oriented measure intended to provide financial support to the family of a deceased employee.
At the same time, the Court said: “Nevertheless, the beneficial character of a scheme does not mean the court can disregard its express terms.”
Where a scheme lays down a specific procedure for exercising the option, fixes a deadline and sets out related financial requirements, the Court said those conditions form an integral part of the scheme.

briefs.headline: Foundries in Coimbatore register 20% growth amid rising demand
briefs.bodyText:
The foundry industry in Coimbatore saw 20 % growth in the last one year with robust orders, said Jayakumar Ramdass, chairman - Inter Foundry and Inter Diecast event and Managing Director of Mahendra Pumps, Foundry Division.
The foundry industry in Coimbatore is doing well, as orders have picked up across sectors, from auto and farm equipment to general engineering. Of the 15 million tonnes of annual casting production in the country, 1.5 million tonnes is manufactured in Coimbatore and it is worth almost ₹ 25,000 crore. Castings worth ₹10,000 crore is exported from here every year. “We need to increase Coimbatore’s share in the global market,” he told The Hindu on Tuesday.
Almost 65 % of castings sold out of Coimbatore are machined and hence value addition is also on the rise. Most of the foundries are operating at more than 90 % capacity and at present, demand is higher than supply. However, one of the main challenges for the industry is availability of skilled manpower. Hence, foundries are investing in automation, new technologies, and digital tools to increase productivity and meet the global standards, Mr. Ramdass said.
The third edition of the exhibition for ferrous and non-ferrous foundry industry - Inter Foundry and Inter DieCast - with 315 exhibitors this year will showcase latest technologies, use of AI, and new equipment.
Organised by the Foundries Development Foundation (FDF) and VA Exhibitions at the CODISSIA Trade Fair Complex from September 10 to 12, the event will have 23 exhibitors from China, five from Germany, and four from Italy apart from participants from across the country. It is expected to attract more than 10,000 visitors.
The three-day expo will have a new concurrent event called “Cast Zone” where 25 FDF members will display castings they make. This segment is open only for registered buyers and it has, so far, 60 overseas buyers confirming their visit, Mr. Ramdass added.
Conferences will be organised on strengthening the Indian foundry sector as a global supply base for ferrous and non-ferrous castings and transition in foundry businesses: succession, scaling up and compliance. There will be a panel discussion on magnesium die casting, said a press release from the organisers.

stories.headline: We want to qualify for LA28... that’s our dream: Navneet, Lalremsiami, Savita and Salima
stories.deck: Savita stresses on the importance of staying in the present in the upcoming continental show-piece, while they are keen to build on the positives and end a 44-year wait
stories.bodyText:
The fifth-place finish at the 2026 women’s FIH Hockey World Cup — the best performance ever by an Indian team — deserves praise.
For the players, however, there is no time to celebrate and rest on their laurels, with the Asian Games right around the corner. Onwards and upwards is the theme in the squad, which departed for Japan after completing a training camp at the Sports Authority of India (SAI) campus here.
For forward Navneet Kaur, defender Lalremsiami Hmarzote, goalkeeper Savita Punia and skipper Salima Tete, the goal is clear: to win a first gold at the continental event since 1982.
The players were in an upbeat mood during a media interaction arranged by SAI here. Excerpts:
You had a break of just a week after the World Cup. What did you do during this period?
Navneet: It was not a week’s break; it was a three-day break. We took rest. You have to take care of your recovery, along with your diet. We did go out into the city for a day. For the most part, it was all about taking care of our diet.
Did the players get time to celebrate the fifth-place finish at the World Cup?
Navneet: No, I think celebrations should happen after we win a medal. Of course, we did well to finish fifth, but we wanted to win a medal. The next tournament — the Asian Games — is even more important. We are focused on that. We will celebrate after that.
How much work have you been doing on finishing? Have you done anything different in the last year?
Navneet: Since (head coach) Sjoerd Marijne arrived, we have been focusing on scoring. As strikers, we have been training separately. We have been training for field goals, to create something in the ‘D’, or to create penalty corner chances. We have been training for all that. We have Taeke Taekema with us as the drag-flick coach, but he also helps with hitting. We have been training with him as well.
What is your next target?
Navneet: Our next target is the Asian Games. We have been preparing for it for four years. We will do our best there. Our team has gained a lot of confidence from the World Cup. We will enter the Asian Games with that confidence.
The European teams in the World Cup were very good, and we performed well against them. As a player, you feel good when you have performed well against good teams. Of course, there are good teams in the Asian Games too. There are also a few lower-ranked teams. It is very important to have that belief as a team and as a player. With that belief, we will go to the Asian Games.
Apart from medals, the Asian Games winner also earns an Olympics berth. Is this an added motivation?
Navneet: The World Cup and the Asian Games are equally important. These big tournaments take place only once in four years. From the Asian Games, we can qualify for the Olympics. So this is also important for us.
Savita, you celebrated on the sidelines when fellow goalkeeper Bichu Devi made that last-gasp save against England in the World Cup. Tell us about your camaraderie with Bichu, given that you are a senior and Bichu started as your understudy.
Savita: My general nature is that I like to connect with everyone.
I believe that the more you are connected off the field, the better the connection is on the field. We are each other’s competitors in training. When we play for India, I want to motivate Bichu the best I can. When I am inside the field, Bichu gives me that motivation.
I think we are setting a good example. This is not the first time I am experiencing this. When I was young, Yogita (Bali) was my senior, and I learnt a lot from her. After that, we had Rajani (Etimarpu). Now it is Bichu and me.
Every coach has his own choice. Which goalkeeper will play today? Will I play the whole match today, or will Bichu play? Whatever the case, we push each other in training.
I know that Bichu is a very good goalkeeper. I will push her as much as I can. If I can motivate her, it is good for Indian hockey.
India last won an Asian Games gold in 1982. Looking at this squad, do you believe that the team can go all the way?
Savita: Every player wants to give their best performance in all tournaments. We did get appreciation for our performance in the World Cup, but only we know how sad we were that we could not win a medal. It is not just about putting in the effort for one tournament. It is a four-year effort.
We have won silver and bronze in the past Asian Games. We talk less about winning the gold. We want to qualify for the 2028 LA Olympics. That’s our target. That’s our dream.
It is important to note that other teams are as focused as we are. You have to look at it match by match. In fact, every match is divided into four parts. We want to go all out in those 15 minutes, and then the next 15 minutes and so on.
China is your main challenge in the Asian Games. India recorded a draw against China in the World Cup. Does that boost the confidence?
Savita: It was a very important draw. A lot of people messaged us saying that we defended well. No, it was not just defence. We played attacking hockey. We had more circle entries than them. We created more chances than them. It was very important for us to either win or draw against China.
In the Asia Cup final last year, China defeated us 4-1. So this draw was very important for us because it gave us the belief that if we play good hockey, we can hold them to a draw or even win.
Everyone only talks about China and India. But in the 2018 Asian Games, Japan defeated India in the final.
In the 2022 Asian Games, Korea reached the final. So I think all four teams are good. I know that rankings differ, but every team is a challenge.
Lalremsiami, you are a role model for young women in Mizoram to promote hockey.
Lalremsiami: Yes, there has been an impact, especially after our fourth-place finish at the 2020 Tokyo Olympics. The image of Mizoram changed. I could not believe it. When I went home after the Olympics, everyone started talking about hockey. Parents and young kids came to speak to me. They asked me to play hockey with them. I really liked it. I got a lot of motivation from it.
Salima, you are from Jharkhand, which is a powerhouse of Indian hockey. How does it feel to captain the Indian team as a player from Jharkhand?
Salima: Like Lalremsiami said, we got so much love after the Tokyo Olympics. In Jharkhand, there were a lot of people who did not know much about hockey. But after the Tokyo Olympics, everybody knows about it. They understand that hockey is a great platform.
Hockey can give you everything. Hockey has certainly given me everything in life.
My family, my village, everything has changed. It is something we never imagined. It makes me emotional.
Even when I had nothing in my village, I played hockey. Now, people in my village know me. They know my parents. It is a big motivation for me.
I try my best to take hockey to a higher level. I do my best so that youngsters learn from me and get interested in playing hockey.

stories.headline: Aryna Sabalenka keeps third straight US Open title hopes alive
stories.deck: Aryna Sabalenka looked close to losing her title defence and her hopes of staying No. 1 in the world. But she fought back when it mattered most and reached the US Open semifinals for the sixth straight year.
stories.bodyText:
Aryna Sabalenka kept her hopes of winning a third straight US Open title alive after edging Linda Noskova 7-6 (1), 3-6, 7-6 (10-7) in a thrilling quarterfinal on Tuesday.
Sabalenka looked close to losing her title defence and her hopes of staying No. 1 in the world. But she fought back when it mattered most and reached the US Open semifinals for the sixth straight year.
“What a battle. What an incredible player she is and I’m speechless right now because I was pushing myself to the limit in this match, especially in the third set,” Sabalenka said. “I honestly thought that that’s it, the match is over and probably that’s what helped me to kind of like, I don’t know, feel loose and just go after my shots.”
Sabalenka will face either No. 3 Jessica Pegula or No. 26 Emma Navarro in the semifinals on Thursday.
She finished the match with a second-serve ace to beat Wimbledon champion Noskova and move into the last four.
Sabalenka fights back in the third set
Sabalenka was in danger of suffering her earliest US Open exit since 2020 when Noskova broke her serve in the third set and moved 4-2 ahead.
But Sabalenka held serve and then produced one of her best games of the match. 
She broke Noskova at love to level the set at 4-4.
“I just felt at some point in the third set she was definitely serving better than me and putting so much pressure on me,” Sabalenka said. "But I’m glad that I kind of threw that thought away and I was able to focus point by point and, like, literally just trying to build something bigger in that moment.
“I got, not lucky, but I’m happy the way I broke her serve at 3-4. I think I really played a great intensity level of tennis, and that really gave me so much confidence that I still can get the win in this match.”
Sabalenka eventually won the match tiebreak 10-7. She went 2-0 down but moved ahead for good when Noskova double-faulted to make it 4-3. Sabalenka then won the next two points to gain some breathing room.
She avoided her first US Open loss since Coco Gauff beat her in the 2023 final.
Noskova puts up a strong fight
Noskova, the No. 6 seed, had won her first major title at Wimbledon and came close to reaching the US Open semifinals.
She finished with 46 winners and 18 aces, compared with Sabalenka's 42 winners and 12 aces.
Both players looked to finish points quickly, while Sabalenka also showed good speed in chasing down drop shots.
“Being a break up in the third set, it’s not very easy. Also having a little break at the start of the tiebreak in the third one, as well, it’s frustrating, obviously,” Noskova said.
"But at the same time, Aryna, she played the best tennis that she could in those moments, which didn’t really make it easy for me.”
Noskova finished with her best run at the US Open. Before this tournament, she had reached only one Grand Slam quarterfinal, at the 2024 Australian Open.
No. 1 ranking also at stake
Sabalenka came into the US Open after losing in the fourth round in Toronto and Cincinnati. She had also exited Wimbledon at the same stage.
However, she found her form in New York and did not drop a set before reaching the quarterfinals.
Sabalenka needed to win this match to keep alive her hopes of remaining No. 1. She will lose the top ranking, which she has held for 99 consecutive weeks, if No. 2 Elena Rybakina beats Zheng Qinwen on Wednesday to reach the semifinals.
If Rybakina loses, Sabalenka can keep the No. 1 ranking by winning the US Open title.

stories.headline: Dilip Gavit's journey: From losing right arm at five to raising the tricolour on podiums
stories.deck: A childhood accident cost Dilip Gavit his right arm, but it could not take away his ambition. From a tribal hamlet in Nashik to a Commonwealth Games record in Glasgow, the 23-year-old's journey has been shaped by resilience, a life-changing coach and an unlikely switch from the 400m to the 100m. The 23-year-old now aims for glory at the Asian Games.
stories.bodyText:
NEW DELHI: At five, Dilip Mahadu Gavit knew little about the fragility of life. A fall from a tree left him with a serious injury to his right arm, but there was no reason to believe that a childhood accident would alter the course of his life. The wound initially appeared manageable, but it turned septic. What followed was every parent's nightmare. Doctors had no choice but to amputate his arm.
For most, losing an arm at such a tender age could have meant the end of dreams before they had even begun. For Gavit, it became the beginning of a battle he would spend years fighting, one that would eventually take him to a place few could have imagined: the Commonwealth Games podium. Earlier this year in Glasgow, the 23-year-old won gold in the men's 100m T47 final in 10.71 seconds, a Commonwealth Games record, and became the first Indian male para-athlete to win gold at the Games.
For Gavit, though, the medal's significance ran deeper than the timing or the record. He credited his medal to Vaijnath Kale, the coach who spotted Gavit's potential when he was still a boy competing in local races in Maharashtra.
"The first thing that comes to my mind is that the day of my event was 
Guru Purnima
. So, in a way, I gave my guru his gurudakshina that day. That makes me feel very good, and it is something I will always remember," Gavit told TimesofIndia.com on the sidelines of an event organised by (SBI) Life Insurance.
Gavit's CWG final was no textbook 100m victory. His start wasn't the strongest, and by halfway, he looked to be chasing the race rather than controlling it. The explosive runners had established their advantage, while Gavit leaned on qualities built through years of 400m training. As others began to lose momentum, Gavit kept coming. His speed endurance became his advantage. He ate into the gap in the final 40 metres, moved past the runners ahead of him and crossed the line in 10.71 seconds. The Commonwealth Games record was gone, and so was any doubt about whether a 400m athlete could make a serious impact over 100m.
For Gavit, it also vindicated the decision to pursue the event after the 400m was left off the programme. Even after producing the biggest 100m performance of his career, though, he knows there's still work to do.
The guru who shaped Gavit's career
Gavit grew up in Tora Dongri, a tribal hamlet in Nashik, where sporting infrastructure was scarce and opportunities were limited. Gavit used to compete in races at school even when facilities and resources weren't readily available, and his willingness to compete eventually brought him to Kale's attention. Kale, a corporate employee turned coach, was impressed with Gavit and requested his parents to let him train, but due to the family's financial difficulties, he didn't get the green light. Kale was confident that he had found a special talent, and he virtually adopted Dilip.
What followed was more than a conventional coach-athlete relationship. Kale took Gavit into his home and gave him the environment he needed to pursue athletics. For a boy from a village with little access to sport, it changed the trajectory of his life. Gavit has never forgotten it.
"I come from a small village where there aren't many facilities, especially when it comes to sport. To take me from there and keep me at his home is something not many people would do. He did that for me. For me, he has been like God," he reminisced.
The switch from 400m to 100m in Glasgow
Kale began moulding him primarily as a 400m runner, an event that demands far more than raw speed. A successful one-lap athlete has to understand pace, conserve energy through the middle stages, and still have enough left to attack the final 100m.
Gavit's progress soon took him beyond para-athletics. Gavit competed in open competitions, regularly holding his own against able-bodied athletes. He reached the Under-20 400m final at the open nationals in 2021 and was part of Maharashtra's bronze-medal 4x400m relay team at the 2022 Khelo India Youth Games.
His move into international para-athletics took him to the 2022 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou, where he won 400m gold, establishing him as one of India's leading para sprinters. Glasgow would require something different, and interestingly, he did not arrive at the 2026 Commonwealth Games as a 100m specialist. If one event defined the youngster, it was the 400m.
On a wet track in Glasgow, though, it was the shortest sprint that gave him the biggest moment of his career. He wasn't among the leaders for much of the race. The pure sprinters' explosiveness had put him behind early, but things changed in the closing stages. Drawing on the speed endurance he has built as a 400m runner, Gavit surged through the final stretch and swept past his rivals.
The absence of the 400m from the Commonwealth Games programme left Gavit with a choice. Rather than miss the Games altogether, he turned to the 100m, an event he was already running as part of his preparation for the longer sprint. The shift wasn't as sudden as it may have looked from outside. Kale had been preparing him for the 100m for years.
"The preparation for the 100m did not start this year. It has actually been going on for the last four years," Kale told this website. "As you saw, he competed in the 100m at the 2023 Asian Para Games in Hangzhou. He reached the quarter-finals and semi-finals, but unfortunately, he fouled in the final and was disqualified."
That foul stayed with Gavit. He'd already won a 400m medal at those Asian Games, but the 100m disappointment bothered him. "My coach had actually started preparing me for the 100m much earlier, in 2022. At the Asian Games, I fouled in the 100m, so I could not finish the event. I won a medal in the 400m there, but I still felt bad about the 100m because of the foul," he said.
That made Glasgow personal. "So when I won the Commonwealth Games gold in the 100m, it felt really good," he added.
There was a practical reason for the switch too. "We have been training for both events in parallel. Since the 400m was not part of the Commonwealth Games programme, we focused on qualifying for and competing in the 100m," Kale explained.
India's Dilip Mahadu Gavit, right, gold medallist, and Mohammed Basil Morssinganakath (PTI photo)
'Still a 400m runner'
The irony of Gavit's CWG triumph is that despite winning one of the most prestigious sprint titles in Indian para-athletics, Kale doesn't see him as a 100m specialist. "He is still primarily a 400m athlete. But his performance in the 100m has also been very good," Kale said.
The 100m and 400m are both sprint events, but the demands differ fundamentally: one is a battle for explosive acceleration and maximum velocity, while the other is about combining speed with the ability to sustain it over an entire lap.
"The 100m is a sprint and demands speed, while the 400m is a speed-endurance event. Balancing the two is quite difficult, but fortunately, we have been managing both very well, and the results have also been very good."
Gavit sees the difference clearly himself. "In the 400m, the focus is much greater because you have to plan the entire race. You have to know how to run the first 100m, how to maintain your pace through the middle of the race and then give everything you have in the final stretch," he said.
"In the 100m, you just have to run hard and the race is over quickly. I actually enjoy the 100m because it finishes so quickly."
There's something amusing in that: the athlete who has just conquered the Commonwealth 100m is still happiest thinking of himself as a 400m runner, while his coach tries to make sure both versions of Gavit keep developing.
The laurels he wants next
Gavit believes the Glasgow conditions cost him something. "The climate there was not very good, and because of that, my start was a little slow. That is something I want to improve."
A Commonwealth gold and a Games record might have been enough for most athletes to sit back and enjoy. Gavit is already looking at the next benchmark. "I want to break the Commonwealth Games record again in 2030."
Before then comes a more immediate challenge. The Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya will demand that Gavit quickly switch gears from 100m preparation back to the 400m, and after two months of concentrating heavily on the shorter sprint, Kale knows the transition won't be straightforward.
"It is definitely a little difficult at the moment because our entire focus has been on the 100m for the last two months. Now, suddenly, we have to shift our focus back towards the 400m. So there are some challenges." But the target is clear. "There is no doubt that we will give our best, and our commitment will be to win medals for India in both events."
Gavit wants more than medals. He wants gold in both. "At the next Asian Games, I want to compete in both the 100m and 400m and win gold in both."

stories.headline: Back to blue for India’s hockey players at the Asian Games
stories.deck: The saffron kit, which led to allegations of politicisation and internal tussle within Hockey India, will be the second option
stories.bodyText:
The Indian hockey teams’ experiment with a change in jersey colour has been partially rolled back and the players will now don the traditional blue at the upcoming Asian Games.
The saffron kit, which led to allegations of politicisation and internal tussle within Hockey India, will be the second option.
“The Indian Olympic Association (IOA) had asked us our preferred choice and HI has given blue as the first choice. Saffron will be the second colour,” HI president Dilip Tirkey said.
Meanwhile, almost two months after the sports ministry asked the Indian Olympic Association to conduct an independent inquiry into former captain Asunta Lakra’s allegations of harassment and intimidation against Hockey India secretary Bholanath Singh, a four-member committee has been constituted for the same.
The committee
The committee, headed by Justice (retd.) Deepa Sharma, also includes former India striker and 2002 Commonwealth Games gold medallist Mamta Kharab and former sprinter Vandana Rao.
Supreme Court advocate Sitwat Nabi is the fourth member of the committee which is expected to begin work later this week.

briefs.headline: Why Cristiano Ronaldo wasn’t nominated for the 2026 Ballon d’Or
briefs.deck: Cristiano Ronaldo has missed the Ballon d’Or shortlist for a fourth straight year despite scoring 28 Saudi league goals, winning the title with Al-Nassr and scoring three World Cup goals. His omission comes as Saudi-based teammates Sadio Mané and Julián Quiñones were nominated, raising questions over how voters weighed Ronaldo’s numbers against other criteria, narratives and competition level.
briefs.bodyText:
Cristiano Ronaldo has missed out on the Ballon d'Or shortlist for a fourth consecutive year, despite leading Al-Nassr to a long-awaited domestic title and producing another strong individual campaign for both club and country.
The omission is particularly intriguing because the 2026 30-player shortlist does include two players from the Saudi Roshn League — Ronaldo's Al-Nassr team-mate Sadio Mané and Al-Qadsiah forward Julián Quiñones.
So while Ronaldo's exclusion may not be exactly unprecedented, depending on who you ask, the presence of two players from the same league inevitably raises a question: what, exactly, separated the nominated pair from the five-time Ballon d'Or winner?
Ronaldo's Saudi League problem has followed him for four years
The 2026 Ballon d’Or nominees were announced by France Football on Tuesday, with Ronaldo once again absent from the initial list of contenders. His longtime rival Lionel Messi, meanwhile, was nominated for the 17th time, with the Argentine representing MLS as the league’s only nominee.
It is the fourth consecutive year that the Portuguese superstar has failed to receive a nomination.
That represents a striking change from earlier in his career. Ronaldo had appeared on the initial Ballon d'Or shortlist for 18 consecutive years, beginning in 2005 and continuing through his most recent nomination in 2022.
His exclusion from the shortlist began after his move to Saudi Arabia.
Ronaldo joined Al-Nassr in January 2023, shortly after his Manchester United contract was terminated, and has not appeared among the Ballon d'Or candidates since.
One obvious explanation is the standing of the Saudi Roshn League compared with Europe’s major competitions, with that factor dominating much of the narrative around his candidacy
Ronaldo has continued to produce impressive individual numbers in Saudi Arabia, but the move has taken him away from the European club competitions that traditionally provide some of the strongest platforms for Ballon d'Or contenders.
The league's reputation may be part of the discussion, although its global standing is not as low as some assumptions suggest. As of March 17, 2026, the Saudi Roshn League was ranked 36th in the world by the 
Global Football Rankings
, with a score of 79.3. That places it outside the level of Europe's leading domestic competitions, but it also shows that the league is not being treated as irrelevant or entirely without competitive value.
There is also the issue of major honours.
Ronaldo had previously endured a lengthy trophy drought with Al-Nassr, but that particular argument changed in May 2026, when he finally helped the club win the 2025-26 Saudi Pro League title.
He scored twice in a 4-1 victory over Damac on the final day of the season, a result that officially secured Al-Nassr's first Saudi league title in seven years.
It was Ronaldo's first major domestic league trophy with the Riyadh club, ending his major official trophy drought in Saudi Arabia.
And Ronaldo was not merely a passenger in that success.
He scored 28 goals in the Roshn League, finishing second in the scoring charts, five behind Quiñones. Al-Nassr's title was therefore achieved with Ronaldo as one of the principal figures in their campaign.
So why Mané and Quiñones, but not Ronaldo?
This is where Ronaldo's case becomes more complicated.
He cannot point to a stronger league position than the two Saudi-based players who made the list, because both Mané and Quiñones were part of the same competition and both were nominated.
Ronaldo also cannot use the league title alone as a decisive argument. Although he helped Al-Nassr win the championship, Mané was his team-mate in that title-winning side, while Quiñones finished above him in the league's scoring charts.
That does not erase Ronaldo's contribution, but it makes the comparison less straightforward. The voters were clearly willing to recognise performances from the Saudi league, so the issue was not simply that the competition was outside Europe.
Julián Quiñones received his first Ballon d'Or nomination after his debut season in the Saudi league. The Mexican forward finished as the competition's top scorer with Al-Qadsiah, scoring 33 goals, 5 more than Ronaldo's.
His strongest argument, however, extended beyond his club form.
Quiñones also impressed at the 2026 World Cup, scoring four goals and providing one assist for Mexico.
Mexico were eliminated in the round of 16, the same stage at which Portugal's campaign ended.
Ronaldo scored three goals at the World Cup before Portugal's elimination, meaning the gap between the two was not overwhelming on the international stage either.
But Quiñones had the edge in the Saudi scoring race, while Ronaldo's advantage came through Al-Nassr's title success. Since both players had a major part of their case built in the same league, the voters may have viewed Quiñones' scoring award and World Cup output as the more persuasive overall package.
The other Saudi-based nominee, meanwhile, is Ronaldo's own team-mate.
Sadio Mané scored just 10 goals and provided six assists in the Roshn League last season, numbers that were considerably lower than Ronaldo's 28 league goals.
Yet Mané's international résumé appears to have strengthened his case.
He helped Senegal reach the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations final and subsequently win the tournament, although the Confederation of African Football later stripped Senegal of the title following an administrative decision that ruled the team had forfeited the match because the players temporarily walked off the pitch in protest of a late penalty.
Mané's 2026 World Cup campaign was less impressive. He failed to score and registered one assist as Senegal were eliminated in the round of 32.
Even so, Mané's nomination shows that the voters were not assessing Saudi-based players only through their league statistics. His case was built more heavily around his international contribution, while Quiñones combined a top-scoring season with a productive World Cup.
Ronaldo, meanwhile, had 28 Saudi league goals, an Al-Nassr league title and three World Cup goals. His numbers were stronger than Mané’s domestically, but the voting appeared to have favoured certain narratives and other criteria beyond the numbers.
Ronaldo's 2025 case makes the omission even more curious
There is another reason the current omission has attracted attention: Ronaldo's failure to make the 2025 Ballon d'Or shortlist came despite a similarly strong résumé.
That year, he had helped Portugal win the 2025 UEFA Nations League, finished as the Saudi Roshn League's top scorer and driven Al-Nassr to third place, behind champions Al-Ittihad and runners-up Al-Hilal.
Even that combination was not enough to earn him a nomination.
After being left off the 2025 shortlist, Ronaldo broke his silence and criticised the award, describing the Ballon d'Or as “fictitious.”
The comment made clear that he did not view the omission as a neutral reflection of his season. It also added another layer to the debate around his relationship with the award, particularly after his move away from European football.
How is the Ballon d'Or criteria measured?
But the Ballon d'Or was never just about domestic stats, one trophy, or where a team finished in the league. France Football actually judges it on three things: how a player performed individually, what their team achieved together, and how they carried themselves on and off the pitch. So league position is only one piece of a much bigger picture, one that also weighs a player's overall influence and consistency across the entire season. And since the award looks at players from anywhere in the world, not just Europe's top leagues, the whole comparison plays out on a global stage.
The voting therefore brings together a player's performances, achievements and profile across the assessment period. The level of competition faced isn't one of the three official criteria, but it still tends to factor into the discussion when voters weigh a player's case, which may help explain why Ronaldo's impressive Saudi numbers have not carried the same weight they once might have when he was competing for Real Madrid or Manchester United.
Still, the Saudi league cannot be treated as an automatic disqualifier. Quiñones and Mané have both made the list, which means the voters were willing to recognise performances from the competition when they felt the wider case was strong enough.
Ronaldo's problem, then, may have less to do with one missing achievement than with how his whole season stacked up against everyone else in the running, once performances, team success, competition level and conduct are all weighed together. The criteria may apply to him as fairly as anyone else on the shortlist, but the numbers tell their own story: Ronaldo hasn't been nominated a single time since he left European football for Saudi Arabia in 2023, no matter how strong his season has been.
Ronaldo's Ballon d'Or legacy remains unmatched
Whatever the reason for his latest omission, Ronaldo remains one of the most frequently nominated players in the history of the award.
He has appeared on the initial Ballon d'Or shortlist 18 times, more than any other player.
That puts him one nomination ahead of Lionel Messi, his great rival across an era of football dominated by the pair.
Italy and AC Milan legend Paolo Maldini is third on the list with 13 nominations, while Johan Cruyff, Franz Beckenbauer and Karim Benzema have each been nominated 12 times.
Ronaldo's most recent nomination came in 2022, after which his name disappeared from the list following his move to Al-Nassr.
The 2026 shortlist does, however, contain a representation of Saudi football through Mané and Quiñones, while Messi is the sole representative of the American league.
The wider 30-man list is dominated by players from Europe's major competitions, with Spain's World Cup-winning squad heavily represented and several Paris Saint-Germain players included after their Champions League triumph during the 2025-26 season.
Ronaldo's numbers and achievements give him a credible case, particularly after Al-Nassr's league title. But the shortlist reflects the voters' preference for other combinations of individual form, international impact, club success and competition level. The fact that Mané and Quiñones were selected shows that Saudi-based players were not ruled out; Ronaldo's case simply did not make the final 30 this time.

briefs.headline: Messi eyes second Spanish club takeover, agrees 100% Eldense buyout
briefs.deck: Lionel Messi is reportedly set to buy 100% of Spanish second-tier club Eldense, expanding his growing football ownership portfolio after acquiring Cornellà earlier this year. The 39-year-old has agreed a deal in principle, with due diligence and Spanish sports authorities’ approval still required before completion. The takeover would give Messi direct control of a professional Spanish football…
briefs.bodyText:
Lionel Messi
 is reportedly preparing for another major step into football ownership, with the Argentina legend set to expand his business interests in Spain after making his first investment in the country's lower leagues earlier this year.
The move would give the 39-year-old a direct stake in Spanish professional football while also taking him closer to the country where he spent the vast majority of his playing career and where he is expected to live after eventually ending his time as an active player with Inter Miami.
Messi reportedly agrees deal to take full control of Eldense
According to 
Marca
, Messi has reached an agreement in principle with the current owners of CD Eldense to acquire the Alicante-based club.
The reports state that Messi would acquire 100 per cent of Eldense's shares, meaning the investment would be made solely by the Argentine and would not involve partners, former players or other third parties.
However, the agreement has not yet been completed.
The deal is expected to be finalised in the coming days, provided the remaining legal and contractual formalities are completed. Those procedures include the necessary financial due diligence, while the proposed takeover will also require approval from the Spanish National Sports Council (CSD).
The club is based in Elda, in Alicante province, and currently competes in LaLiga 2, Spain's second division. 
Eldense were recently promoted to the Segunda División, also known as LaLiga Hypermotion, for the 2026–27 season after winning Group 2 of the Primera Federación in May 2026, according to reports. The club currently has around 3,500 season-ticket holders.
The proposed acquisition would represent another piece of Messi's emerging football business portfolio.
Earlier in 2026, Messi acquired 100 per cent of the shares in UE Cornellà, a Catalan club competing in the Spanish third tier. That deal was announced in April, with Cornellà saying Messi's arrival would begin “a new chapter in the club’s history” aimed at driving sporting and institutional growth, strengthening its foundations and continuing investment in talent.
The project at Cornellà has placed particular emphasis on youth academy development and women's football.
The Eldense investment would take Messi's involvement to a considerably higher level of the Spanish football pyramid, with the club competing in professional football.
The reports suggest the motivation behind the project is Messi's desire to invest his footballing legacy back into the game itself, with Eldense's location also potentially fitting into his longer-term plans.
Elda is in Alicante province and is relatively close to Catalonia, where Messi is expected to live after his playing career comes to an end.
Eldense takeover comes as club searches for new manager
Eldense was previously acquired by an international investment group with Colombian roots, led by businessman Juan Carlos Trujillo, who bought the club from Pascual Pérez in October 2015.
There had already been speculation over a possible change of ownership in recent months, with Argentine businessman Ricardo Pini reportedly linked with a potential takeover worth around €12million.
Messi's reported agreement has now changed the picture considerably, although the final transaction still needs to clear its remaining requirements before it can be considered complete.
The club is also experiencing difficulties on the pitch
Eldense dismissed Claudio Barragán on Monday, making him the first Segunda División manager to be sacked this season, according to reports.
The club had collected just two points from its opening four league matches and had not appointed a replacement at the time of reporting.
Messi's potential arrival would therefore come while Eldense attempts to stabilise both its sporting and institutional situation.
The proposed takeover also marks another intriguing development in Messi's post-playing career.
The Argentine, who is now 39, has already won virtually every major honour available to him, including the World Cup and Champions League, and has collected a record eight Ballon d'Or awards.
His investment in Cornellà earlier this year signalled his growing interest in football away from the pitch. A takeover of Eldense would represent a substantially larger commitment, putting one of the game's greatest-ever players in position to influence a club competing in Spain's professional second tier.
For now, though, the key distinction is that Messi has reportedly reached an agreement in principle, rather than completed the acquisition.
The final legal and contractual procedures, including due diligence and the required CSD authorisation, still need to be completed before Messi can officially take control of Eldense.

briefs.headline: Yamal sets Ballon d’Or record: Teen earns historic third nomination before 20
briefs.deck: Lamine Yamal has made Ballon d’Or history by becoming the first player to earn three nominations before turning 20. The Barcelona star, nominated in 2024, 2025 and 2026, finished eighth before rising to second last year. His latest recognition follows another outstanding season, including La Liga success with Barcelona and a World Cup triumph with Spain.
briefs.bodyText:
Lamine Yamal has made Ballon d'Or history after becoming the first player ever to receive three nominations for the prestigious award before turning 20.
The Barcelona forward was included in the 30-player shortlist for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, announced on September 8, giving him a nomination for the third consecutive year after also making the shortlist in 2024 and 2025.
Yamal, who was born on July 13, 2007, in Mataró, Spain, is still only 19, but has already established himself as one of the most prominent players in world football for both FC Barcelona and Spain.
The achievement is different from simply being nominated multiple times. Legendary figures including Cristiano Ronaldo and Lionel Messi have been nominated for the Ballon d'Or numerous times, while Yamal's distinction is the age at which he has accumulated his three nominations.
He was also the youngest player ever nominated for the Ballon d'Or, breaking into the shortlist at just 17 years old in 2024.
Yamal has now been nominated three years in a row
Yamal's first Ballon d'Or nomination came in 2024, when he finished eighth in the voting after playing a key role in Spain's victory at the 2024 European Championship.
A year later, he went even closer to winning the award.
Yamal finished second in the 2025 Ballon d'Or, behind Paris Saint-Germain winger Ousmane Dembele, who had enjoyed a treble-winning campaign.
His third consecutive nomination follows another outstanding season for both club and country.
For Barcelona, Yamal scored 24 goals and provided 15 assists in 45 games across all competitions, helping Hansi Flick's side successfully defend their La Liga and Supercopa de España titles.
He then played a significant role in Spain's victorious 2026 FIFA World Cup campaign in the United States, Canada and Mexico.
Yamal featured in all seven matches of Spain's run to the World Cup title and scored, and assisted once apiece during the tournament. Spain defeated 10-man defending champions Argentina in the final in New Jersey in July to win their second World Cup.
That success has added further weight to Yamal's case for the 2026 Ballon d'Or, after he had already collected major honours at both club and international level.
His club honours include three La Liga titles in 2023, 2025 and 2026, as well as the 2025 domestic treble.
Individually, he has won the Kopa Trophy in both 2024 and 2025, making him the only player in football history to win the award for the world's best young player in consecutive years, making him the only player in football history to win the award for the world's best young player in consecutive years.
Yamal has already rewritten Spain's record books
Yamal's record-breaking Ballon d'Or achievement is only the latest in a series of milestones he has reached at an extraordinarily young age.
He has earned 33 caps for Spain's senior national team and scored seven goals, having become an established figure for La Roja before his 20th birthday.
His international career began with another historic achievement.
Yamal became Spain's youngest-ever player and youngest-ever goalscorer when he made his senior debut against Georgia on September 8, 2023, aged just 16 years and 57 days.
He went on to win the Euro 2024, the 2025 UEFA Nations League and the 2026 World Cup with Spain.
His World Cup campaign also saw him start all seven matches as Spain completed their historic run to the title, making him one of the youngest World Cup winners in football history.
The 2026 Ballon d'Or nomination comes after an equally impressive start to the new club season.
Yamal drew a blank as Barcelona began their campaign with a 5-0 victory at Elche and again in the 2-0 home win over Athletic Club, before scoring twice in a 3-2 home victory over Rayo Vallecano.
He then scored another two goals as Barcelona defeated Valencia 5-0 away from home at the weekend, a result that moved Flick's side three points clear at the top of the fledgling La Liga standings.
Barcelona's Lamine Yamal celebrates after scoring his side's second goal during a Spanish La Liga soccer match between Barcelona and Rayo Vallecano in Barcelona, Spain, Monday, Aug. 31, 2026. (AP Photo/Joan Monfort)
Barcelona's next challenge is against Feyenoord at home on September 9, 10:15 PM IST, as they begin their quest for a first UEFA Champions League title in more than a decade.
Yamal's third Ballon d'Or nomination therefore arrives at a remarkable point in his career. He has already been the youngest nominee in the award's history, finished eighth and then second, won back-to-back Kopa Trophies, collected major domestic and international honours and helped Spain become world champions.
Now, before even turning 20, he has become the first player ever to receive three Ballon d'Or nominations at that age.
The 2026 ceremony will take place on Monday, October 26, 2026, at the London Palladium Theatre in London, marking the first time the Ballon d'Or ceremony will be held outside Paris.
Alongside Yamal, the 30-player shortlist features leading names including defending winner Ousmane Dembélé, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappé and 39-year-old Lionel Messi, with the winner set to be crowned in London.
For Yamal, however, the nomination itself has already secured another unique place in Ballon d'Or history.

briefs.headline: Liverpool to replace Standard Chartered with Turkish Airlines in £300m+ shirt deal
briefs.deck: Liverpool have agreed a reported £300million-plus, five-year sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines, replacing Standard Chartered as the club’s principal and front-of-shirt partner from 2027. The deal, reportedly worth more than £60million annually, ends Standard Chartered’s 17-year shirt sponsorship. Turkish Airlines branding will feature on Liverpool’s men’s, women’s and academy shirts, making…
briefs.bodyText:
Liverpool have agreed a five-year sponsorship deal with Turkish Airlines worth more than £300million, with the airline set to become the club's new principal partner and front-of-shirt sponsor from next season.
The agreement, which is reported to be worth in excess of £60million a year, will bring an end to Liverpool's 17-year relationship with Standard Chartered and see Turkish Airlines branding appear on the shirts of the men's, women's and academy teams from June 1, 2027.
Liverpool believe the deal ranks among the most lucrative front-of-shirt agreements in Premier League history, with reports suggesting its value is comparable to major deals struck by Manchester United and Manchester City.
The exact financial terms have not been disclosed by Liverpool, but media reports have valued the five-year package at more than £300million ($405.78million).
Turkish Airlines replaces Standard Chartered after 17 years
The partnership marks a significant change to Liverpool's commercial identity, with Standard Chartered's 17-year run as the club's lead shirt sponsor coming to an end.
However, Standard Chartered will not be leaving Liverpool altogether. The financial services company will remain involved as a Global Partner, while Turkish Airlines takes over the primary position in the club's commercial branding.
The new agreement will also make Turkish Airlines only the third new front-of-shirt sponsor Liverpool have had in 35 years.
Carlsberg occupied the front of Liverpool's shirts from 1992 until 2010, before Standard Chartered began its 17-year association with the club.
Liverpool's most recent deal with Standard Chartered was understood to be worth around £50million per year, meaning the reported Turkish Airlines agreement represents a substantial increase.
Liverpool's Virgil van Dijk reacts during the English Premier League soccer match between Ipswich Town and Liverpool in Ipswich, England, Friday, Sept. 4, 2026. (AP Photo/Dave Shopland)
Liverpool chief commercial officer Ben Latty welcomed the new partnership and highlighted the connection between the club and Turkey.
“This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027,” Latty said.
“The front of the Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club. Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network, and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005.”
Latty's reference was to one of the most famous nights in Liverpool's history — the 2005 Champions League final in Istanbul, when Rafael Benitez's side famously came from 3-0 down against AC Milan before winning on penalties in what became known as the 'Miracle of Istanbul'.
The new arrangement also expands Turkish Airlines' already significant presence in football. The airline is an official Champions League partner and the main sponsor of Turkey's national team.
Turkish Airlines flies to more airports around the world than any of its competitors and is expected to make a major financial investment in its partnership with Liverpool.
Liverpool's global reach behind record commercial deal
The agreement comes as Liverpool continue to emphasise the enormous global reach of their brand.
The club believes that one Liverpool shirt is sold somewhere in the world every 20 seconds, while it also claims to have more standalone retail stores than any other football club.
Liverpool recently expanded that retail network by opening a new store on Oxford Street in London.
That international footprint is particularly relevant to a partnership with Turkish Airlines, whose own network spans a huge number of destinations around the world.
The five-year agreement will therefore place Turkish Airlines prominently across Liverpool's men's, women's and academy teams, beginning with the 2027-28 season.
For Liverpool, it represents a major commercial upgrade while ending one of the longest-running shirt sponsorship relationships in the Premier League.
For Turkish Airlines, meanwhile, the deal provides a prominent association with one of the world's most recognisable football clubs and builds on its existing involvement with the Champions League and Turkish national team.
The partnership will formally begin on June 1, 2027, when Turkish Airlines takes over the principal position from Standard Chartered.

briefs.headline: Asian Games | Make the occasion remember you: Usha at official send-off
briefs.deck: The official contingent jersey was unveiled in the ceremony where kabbadi player Sehrawat was present along with CWG gold medallist judoka Asmita and weightlifter Gyaneshwari
briefs.bodyText:
The official send-off ceremony for India’s Asian Games contingent was held here on Tuesday with several athletes, coaches and officials present on the occasion.
While several top names were missing due to various reasons — the Indian hockey teams have already left for Aichi-Nagoya while the rifle and pistol shooters are training in Bhopal — kabaddi captain Pawan Sehrawat was present along with Commonwealth Games gold medallist judoka Asmita Dey and weightlifter Gyaneshwari Yadav among others.
The event was attended by sports minister Mansukh Mandaviya, Indian Olympic Association president P.T. Usha and officials travelling with the Indian contingent.
“There is no shortage of talent in this country. We have to change the pressure into performance and opportunity into achievement,” Mandaviya said.
Don’t be overwhelmed
“I am confident because our athletes have prepared well. Do not be overwhelmed by the occasion; make the occasion remember you.
“Go out there, enjoy the competition, and give everything you have. Go with confidence, courage, humility and the belief that you can compete with anyone in Asia,” Usha added. The official contingent jersey was also unveiled on the occasion.
The Asian Games will be held in Aichi-Nagoya from September 19 to October 4 with 503 athletes representing India across 36 sporting disciplines.
BCCI president Mithun Manhas and vice-president Rajeev Shukla were also present and confirmed that the cricketers would be staying at official accommodations only.

briefs.headline: Indian Railways in the fray in FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia
briefs.bodyText:
Reigning National champion Indian Railways will be competing in the third edition of Asia’s premier annual competition for women’s basketball clubs (FIBA-Women’s Basketball League Asia-WBLA) to be held at the Sree Kanteerava Stadium in Bengaluru from October 20 to 25. Railways will take on Denso Iris (Japan) in its first match on October 21. This is the first time a team from India is taking part in WBLA.
Six teams have been divided into two groups according to the FIBA World Ranking for Women. The Group Phase, to be held on October 20-22, will be played in a single round-robin format.
The top two teams from each group will compete in the knockout crossover semifinals, while the teams that will finish third in their groups will play in a Classification 5-6. These games will be played on October 24 followed by the final on October 25.
“Our team looks good. We have to start the preparatory camp which will either be in Telangana or Bengaluru. It’s quite a tough pool we are in with clubs from Korea and Japan. We will give a tough fight and hope for the best,” P. Anitha, head coach of the Indian team told The Hindu here on Tuesday.
The groups:
A: Sichuan Yuanda Meile (China); Akari Sparks (Philippines); Cathay Life Tigers (Taipei); B: Denso Iris (Japan); KB Stars (Korea); Indian Railways.

briefs.headline: Ballon d’Or shortlist: Dembélé, Mbappé, Kane, Messi, Yamal lead star-studded race
briefs.deck: The race for the 2026 Ballon d'Or is officially underway, featuring a dazzling array of talent. Defending champion Ousmane Dembélé is set to clash with fierce rivals like Kylian Mbappé, Harry Kane, and the legendary Lionel Messi. Meanwhile, the women's award faces a shift in dynamics following Aitana Bonmatí's absence. The winners will be announced during a glamorous ceremony in London on October…
briefs.bodyText:
The race for the 2026 Ballon d’Or has officially begun, with defending champion Ousmane Dembélé, Kylian Mbappé, 
Harry Kane
, 
Lionel Messi
 and Lamine Yamal among the biggest names included in the 30-player men’s shortlist announced by France Football on Tuesday.
The women’s shortlist also features a host of major contenders, with two-time winner Alexia Putellas, Ewa Pajor and Melchie Dumornay among those hoping to succeed Aitana Bonmatí, who has won the award in each of the past three years but missed much of the season through injury.
The winners will be crowned at a ceremony in London on October 26, with the event moving away from its traditional Paris setting to mark the 70th anniversary of the first Ballon d’Or, won by England legend Stanley Matthews in 1956.
For Dembélé, the opportunity to become the first player since Bonmatí to retain the award comes after another remarkable season with Paris Saint-Germain. The Frenchman helped PSG win a second consecutive Champions League title, strengthening his claim to remain at the top of the individual game.
Yet even Dembélé believes the trophy could stay in Paris regardless of who eventually wins it.
“I don't think the trophy is undecided. I think it will remain in the hands of a Paris Saint-Germain player," he said in an interview with France Football.
When asked to name his three leading contenders, Dembélé selected PSG teammate Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Kane and Mbappé. He also highlighted Michael Olise, Yamal, Fabian Ruiz and Willian Pacho — but notably left himself out of his own top three.
Mbappé believes this could finally be his year
Mbappé enters the race having produced one of the most prolific individual campaigns of his career, despite Real Madrid ending the season without a major trophy.
The France captain scored 42 goals in 44 appearances for Madrid and also enjoyed a record-breaking World Cup campaign. He claimed the Golden Boot for a second consecutive time with 10 goals and moved beyond Lionel Messi to become the tournament’s all-time leading scorer with 22 goals.
His individual numbers have strengthened his belief that he could finally get his hands on the Ballon d’Or after finishing third in 2023.
“There are many people who speak about me and the Ballon d’Or. Of course I’ve made history in the most important competition. Maybe it’s a good year for this, but people can vote according to what they think,” Mbappé said on Monday.
The French superstar also acknowledged the unique expectations that come with playing for Real Madrid.
“I think when you play for Real Madrid, the best club in the world, people automatically associate you with this award,” Mbappé added. “I always think I’m the best, but everyone is entitled to their own opinion.”
Asked about comparisons with other leading contenders, Mbappé refused to get drawn into a debate that could quickly become endless.
“I don’t like making comparisons because I do a lot of things that others don’t," Mbappé said. "If we get into that it becomes an endless debate, you know?”
Kane, Yamal and Messi among the contenders
Kane has arguably produced one of the strongest seasons of his career, scoring 73 goals for club and country and finally adding major silverware to his collection after helping Bayern Munich win the Bundesliga.
Yamal is another major contender after playing a central role in Spain’s World Cup triumph and Barcelona’s La Liga success. His continued rise has put the teenage forward firmly among the game's elite.
Messi, meanwhile, remains on the shortlist at 39. The eight-time winner continues to challenge for individual honours after guiding Argentina to a runner-up finish at the World Cup and helping Inter Miami win Major League Soccer.
Dembélé and Mbappé both featured for France at the World Cup, where they were eliminated by eventual champions Spain in the semi-finals. While major team trophies traditionally carry significant weight in the Ballon d’Or race, Mbappé’s individual World Cup records could keep him firmly in contention.
Bonmatí misses out as women’s race opens up
The women’s award has a notably different complexion this year after Bonmatí was left out of the 30-player shortlist.
The Barcelona star had dominated the award, winning three consecutive Ballon d’Or Feminin titles, but an injury kept her out for much of the season. She returned towards the end of Barcelona’s campaign and was able to feature as the club completed a quadruple that included another Champions League triumph.
Putellas, a two-time winner, now has an opportunity to reclaim the crown, while Pajor and Dumornay are among the other prominent names in the running.
The coaching awards will also be closely watched. World Cup-winning Spain coach Luis de la Fuente and Premier League-winning Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta headline the men's nominees for the Johan Cruyff Trophy.
They are joined by Unai Emery of Aston Villa, Vincent Kompany of Bayern Munich and Luis Enrique of Paris Saint-Germain.
In the women's category, Jonatan Giraldez, Andree Jeglertz, Nils Nielsen, Pere Romeu and Elena Sadiku have been nominated.
How the Ballon d’Or winner is decided
The Ballon d’Or, created by France Football, has been awarded to men since 1956 and to women since 2018. The men's award is voted on by one journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the FIFA rankings, while the women's award involves journalists from the top 50.
Each voter ranks their selections, with points awarded according to the position of each player. The player collecting the most points wins.
Organisers say the voting is based on three criteria, in order of importance: individual performances and decisive, impressive character; collective performances and titles won; and class and fair play.
With the shortlist now confirmed, Dembélé has the chance to defend his crown, Mbappé is chasing the first Ballon d’Or of his career, Kane is hoping his trophy-laden season can finally translate into individual recognition, while Yamal and Messi add further star power to a race that promises to go down to the wire.

briefs.headline: Duleep Trophy final | East bowlers have South on the mat
briefs.deck: The host loses six wickets for 242, with 466 runs still in arrears at the end of day three; only Padikkal and Tilak, who is batting on 56, offer some resistance; Shami and Mukesh scalp two wickets for the visitor
briefs.bodyText:
A disciplined bowling performance and the comfort of a huge first-innings total ensured East Zone tightened its stranglehold over South Zone on day three of the Duleep Trophy final at the MAC Stadium here.
Chasing 709, South needed more than a couple of batters to produce special knocks. Unfortunately, aside from Devdutt Padikkal (62, 104b, 4x4), none of the others showed much inclination to keep the contest alive.
In the final session on Tuesday, skipper Tilak Varma offered some resistance, remaining unbeaten on 56 (133b, 5x4), but it was akin to trying to keep a sinking boat afloat as his side finished on 242 for six, still 466 runs in arrears.
For East, Mohammed Shami and Mukesh Kumar took two wickets each. The former showed that he can still make the ball talk through both conventional and reverse swing with short yet incisive spells.
After losing opener Ricky Bhui early — caught down the leg-side off Mukesh Kumar — N. Jagadeesan and Padikkal added 60 runs for the second wicket.
The TN ’keeper-batter, though, threw away his start, slicing an innocuous wide delivery from left-arm spinner Shikhar Mohan to backward point.
Padikkal, fresh from twin centuries in the recently concluded Test series in Sri Lanka, was at his fluent best, cruising to a half-century. The southpaw looked set for another big one, until he flicked a leg-side half-volley from Mukesh down the square-leg fielder’s throat, much to his disbelief.
Shami, in his second spell, attacked the stumps relentlessly and reaped the rewards through his trademark delivery that seamed off the pitch and trapped Shaik Rasheed plumb in front.
The 36-year-old then produced another peach from around the wicket that nipped away just enough to have R. Smaran caught behind, leaving South tottering at 174 for five.
Tilak and Shreyas Gopal then added 66 for the sixth wicket before the latter was dismissed in the final over of the day. With East skipper Ishan Kishan already hinting that his team was not inclined to enforce the follow-on, the next two days could well be about going through the formalities before the coronation.
